title: Temporally Multimode Ion-Ion Entanglement Over 1.2 Kilometer Fibers
authors: Z.-B. Cui, Z.-Q. Wang, P.-Y. Liu, Y. Wang, P.-C. Lai, J.-X. Shi, Y.-D. Sun, Z.-C. Tian, H.-S. Sun, Y.-B. Liang, B.-X. Qi, Y.-Y. Huang, Z.-C. Zhou, Y.-K. Wu, Y. Xu, Y.-F. Pu, And L.-M. Duan

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020803] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of temporally multiplexed ion-ion entanglement over 1.2 km fibers, a key step toward quantum repeaters.
motivation: Building large-scale quantum networks requires long-distance entanglement distribution; ion traps are promising but face challenges in generating and distributing entanglement over fiber.
method: Trapped Yb+ ions are entangled via a photonic interface, and the entanglement is temporally multiplexed to overcome loss and decoherence in 1.2 km fiber links.
result: High-fidelity ion-ion entanglement is achieved over 1.2 km fibers with temporal multiplexing, demonstrating a viable approach for quantum repeater nodes.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum networks by showing that trapped ions can serve as long-distance entanglement sources with multiplexing, enabling scalable quantum communication.

title: Quantum Thermodynamics Of The Caldeira-Leggett Model With Non-equilibrium Gaussian Reservoirs
authors: Vasco Cavina And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2136 (2026).

We introduce a non-equilibrium version of the Caldeira-Leggett model in which a quantum particle is strongly coupled to a set of engineered reservoirs. The reservoirs are composed by collections of squeezed and displaced thermal modes, in contrast to the standard case in which the modes are assumed to be at equilibrium. The model proves to be very versatile. Strongly displaced/squeezed reservoirs can be used to generate an effective time dependence in the system Hamiltonian and can be identified as sources of pure work. In the case of squeezing, the time dependence is stochastic and breaks the fluctuation-dissipation relation, this can be reconciled with the second law of thermodynamics by correctly accounting for the energy used to generate the initial non-equilibrium conditions. To go beyond the average description and compute the full heat statistics, we treat squeezing and displacement as generalized Hamiltonians on a modified Keldysh contour. As an application of this technique, we show the quantum-classical correspondence between the heat statistics in the non-equilibrium Caldeira-Leggett model and the statistics of a classical Langevin particle under the action of squeezed and displaced colored noises. Finally, we discuss thermodynamic symmetries of the heat generating function, proving a fluctuation theorem for the energy balance and showing that the conservation of energy at the trajectory level emerges in the classical limit.

.
tldr: This paper extends the Caldeira-Leggett model to non-equilibrium Gaussian reservoirs, deriving thermodynamic properties and fluctuation theorems for a strongly coupled quantum particle.
motivation: To understand quantum thermodynamics in non-equilibrium settings where reservoirs are squeezed or displaced, and to establish a connection with classical Langevin dynamics.
method: The authors treat squeezing and displacement as generalized Hamiltonians on a modified Keldysh contour, enabling computation of full heat statistics beyond the average.
result: They show that strongly displaced/squeezed reservoirs can generate effective time dependence and pure work, and that the fluctuation-dissipation relation is broken but reconciled with the second law. A quantum-classical correspondence for heat statistics is demonstrated.
conclusion: The model provides a versatile framework for studying quantum thermodynamics with non-equilibrium reservoirs, and the derived fluctuation theorem for energy balance holds in the classical limit.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework that connects mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, addressing systems far from equilibrium.
method: Uses large deviations theory to construct a fluctuation framework for Markov jump processes, deriving thermodynamic laws and fluctuation theorems at the macroscopic scale.
result: Establishes thermodynamically consistent alternatives to traditional Langevin approaches, applicable to chemical reaction networks, electronic circuits, and Potts models.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem.

title: The Apparatus Strikes Back: Momentum Conservation And The Cost Of Spatial Superpositions
authors: Lucas C. C\'eleri, Diogo O. Soares-Pinto, Daniel A. Turolla Vanzella
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Preparing massive particles in coherent spatial superpositions is a central objective of modern quantum science, motivated by applications ranging from fundamental tests of quantum mechanics and gravity to quantum-enhanced sensing. The experimental difficulty of realizing such superpositions is usually attributed to environmental decoherence mechanisms whose impact depends on the details of the experimental implementation. Here we identify a universal constraint arising from momentum conservation and the quantum nature of the preparation apparatus. Any protocol that places a particle of mass [MATH] in a spatial superposition with separation [MATH] necessarily entangles the particle with the center-of-mass degree of freedom of the apparatus responsible for the splitting. The resulting recoil displacement, fixed by conservation of the mass dipole moment, reduces the coherence of the particle when the apparatus is not included as part of the quantum system. For an apparatus of mass [MATH], preserving coherence requires the recoil displacement to remain smaller than the coherence length of the apparatus center-of-mass state, leading to a quantitative bound expressible as a constraint on its temperature and on how rigidly the apparatus is anchored to the laboratory frame. We analyze the implications of this bound for current matter-wave interferometry experiments, proposals for gravitationally mediated entanglement, and tests of quantum mechanics near the Planck scale. Our main result, which may seem counterintuitive, is that the recoil of even heavy macroscopic apparatuses can pose a surprisingly strong constraint on the coherence of spatial superpositions of particles with masses well below the Planck mass. Finally, we discuss why the resulting limitation should be regarded as a conservative estimate and under which conditions it can be interpreted as an instance of false decoherence.
tldr: Momentum conservation during spatial superposition preparation entangles the particle with the apparatus, imposing a universal bound on coherence.
motivation: To identify a fundamental, apparatus-independent constraint on creating spatial superpositions of massive particles, beyond environmental decoherence.
method: Derives a bound from conservation of the mass dipole moment, analyzing the recoil displacement of the apparatus and its effect on coherence.
result: The recoil displacement reduces coherence unless it is smaller than the apparatus's coherence length, leading to a constraint on apparatus temperature and rigidity.
conclusion: Even heavy macroscopic apparatuses impose strong coherence constraints, relevant for matter-wave interferometry and tests of quantum gravity.

title: A Diagrammatic Field Theory Of Quantum Error Correction
authors: Steven Rayan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a field-theoretic framework for quantum error correction centred on fusion-space codes in unitary fusion categories. Admissible clusters determine total-charge sectors and orthogonal footprint projectors recording locally visible data left by error histories. The central distinction is between diagnostic footprint algebras and syndrome-admissible commuting algebras: the latter can be measured without revealing logical information and resolve chosen error representatives into measured sectors. For such algebras, exact correctability is equivalent to fibrewise Knill--Laflamme conditions, yielding a measure-then-recover factorization. Under a contractible-vacuum locality hypothesis, closed neutral composites give a categorical sufficient criterion for scalar action on the code. In the Ising theory, four [MATH] punctures show that pair-charge footprints can be complementary logical diagnostics and realize an exact one-qubit Clifford shadow. A proper six-[MATH] code instead admits a syndrome-admissible pair-charge measurement and exact recovery from an explicit Majorana bilinear error. A second bilinear has the same measured footprint but differs by a logical bit flip, producing a concrete nontrivial footprint fibre and genuine decoding ambiguity. We also formulate conformal-block likelihood data and compute geometry-dependent Ising four-point weights. For growing code families, we prove a conditional Peierls-type threshold theorem: bounded connected-region growth, local stochastic noise, local neutralizability of small residual components, and componentwise decoder balance imply [MATH] below a nonzero constant error rate. We conclude with representation-theoretic and algebro-geometric directions involving tube and Hopf algebras, Yangian-type structures, Higgs bundles, spectral curves, Jacobians, and abelian varieties.
tldr: Develops a field-theoretic framework for quantum error correction using fusion categories and topological order.
motivation: To provide a unified categorical and field-theoretic description of quantum error correction, enabling analysis of correctability and decoding in topological codes.
method: Uses unitary fusion categories to model error correction, defining diagnostic and syndrome-admissible algebras, and derives a categorical Knill-Laflamme condition.
result: Proves a threshold theorem for code families under local stochastic noise and demonstrates the framework on Ising theory examples, including a one-qubit Clifford shadow and decoding ambiguity.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful new perspective on quantum error correction, linking it to topological field theory and algebraic geometry, with potential for new code constructions.

The authors show that exact correctability for such algebras is equivalent to fibrewise Knill-Laflamme conditions, leading to a measure-then-recover factorization. Under a contractible-vacuum locality hypothesis, closed neutral composites provide a categorical sufficient criterion for scalar action on the code. The framework is applied to the Ising anyon theory, where four σ punctures demonstrate that pair-charge footprints can serve as complementary logical diagnostics and realize an exact one-qubit Clifford shadow. A proper six-σ code admits a syndrome-admissible pair-charge measurement and exact recovery from an explicit Majorana bilinear error, while a second bilinear error produces a nontrivial footprint fibre and genuine decoding ambiguity. The paper also formulates conformal-block likelihood data and computes geometry-dependent Ising four-point weights. For growing code families, a conditional Peierls-type threshold theorem is proved: under bounded connected-region growth, local stochastic noise, local neutralizability of small residual components, and componentwise decoder balance, the failure probability satisfies Pr_L(fail) ≤ C|Ω_L|e^{-cL} below a nonzero constant error rate. For the six-σ code, a specific Majorana bilinear error (e.g., γ1γ2) is exactly recoverable via syndrome-admissible measurement, while another bilinear (γ3γ4) produces the same measured footprint but differs by a logical bit flip, creating a nontrivial footprint fibre. title: Quantitative Wigner-Araki-Yanase Theorems For Unitary And Antiunitary Symmetries
authors: Hiroyasu Tajima Akihiro Hokkyo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Symmetry imposes fundamental constraints on quantum measurement and control. The Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorem and its quantitative extensions capture this restriction for continuous symmetries, in terms of fluctuations of conserved generators. Such generator-based bounds, however, do not provide quantitative limitations for discrete unitary symmetries or for antiunitary symmetries. Here we establish quantitative WAY-type theorems for symmetry-breaking projective measurements and unitary gates under arbitrary unitary and antiunitary symmetries. Our approach is based on a two-target no-programming inequality: if a single processor approximately implements two operations that amplify distinguishability, then the corresponding program states must themselves be distinguishable. Applied to symmetric implementations, this converts the error of an asymmetric measurement or gate directly into a lower bound on the asymmetry of the apparatus state, quantified by its fidelity with its symmetry-transformed copy. Our results apply to discrete and antiunitary symmetries, thereby providing a fundamental limit for symmetry-limited quantum measurement and control beyond the continuous-symmetry regime.
tldr: Establishes quantitative Wigner-Araki-Yanase theorems for arbitrary unitary and antiunitary symmetries, extending previous bounds beyond continuous symmetries.
motivation: Previous WAY theorems only covered continuous symmetries; discrete and antiunitary symmetries lacked quantitative limitations, leaving a gap in fundamental constraints on quantum measurement and control.
method: Derives a two-target no-programming inequality that relates the error of an asymmetric operation to the distinguishability of program states, then applies it to symmetric implementations of projective measurements and unitary gates.
result: Provides lower bounds on the asymmetry of the apparatus state (via fidelity with its symmetry-transformed copy) for any symmetry-breaking operation under discrete or antiunitary symmetries.
conclusion: Offers fundamental limits for symmetry-limited quantum measurement and control beyond the continuous-symmetry regime, advancing the theory of quantum information constraints.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper extends the Wigner-Araki-Yanase (WAY) theorem, which quantifies how conservation laws limit quantum measurements, to arbitrary unitary and antiunitary symmetries. The original WAY theorem and its quantitative versions apply only to continuous symmetries, providing bounds based on fluctuations of conserved generators. The authors establish quantitative WAY-type theorems for projective measurements and unitary gates under discrete unitary and antiunitary symmetries. Their approach uses a two-target no-programming inequality: if a single processor approximately implements two operations that amplify distinguishability, then the program states must themselves be distinguishable. Applied to symmetric implementations, this converts the error of an asymmetric measurement or gate into a lower bound on the asymmetry of the apparatus state, quantified by its fidelity with its symmetry-transformed copy. The results cover discrete and antiunitary symmetries, thus providing fundamental limits for symmetry-limited quantum measurement and control beyond the continuous-symmetry regime.
key_contributions: Establishes quantitative WAY-type theorems for projective measurements under arbitrary unitary and antiunitary symmetries.
Establishes quantitative WAY-type theorems for unitary gates under arbitrary unitary and antiunitary symmetries.
Introduces a two-target no-programming inequality as a general tool to derive bounds on asymmetry.
Provides lower bounds on the error of asymmetric operations in terms of the fidelity between the apparatus state and its symmetry-transformed copy.

deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors employ a two-target no-programming inequality, which is a novel conceptual tool. The idea is that if a single quantum processor can approximately implement two different operations that amplify distinguishability (i.e., map orthogonal input states to orthogonal output states), then the program states encoding those operations must themselves be distinguishable. By considering symmetric implementations where the processor is invariant under a symmetry, the authors relate the distinguishability of program states to the asymmetry of the apparatus state. Specifically, they show that the error in implementing an asymmetric operation (measurement or gate) is lower bounded by a function of the fidelity between the apparatus state and its symmetry-transformed version. The proof uses standard quantum information techniques such as fidelity, trace distance, and properties of quantum channels. The analysis is rigorous and covers both unitary and antiunitary symmetries, including time-reversal symmetry.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key results are lower bounds on the error of symmetry-breaking measurements and gates. For a projective measurement that is not symmetric under a symmetry group G, the error (e.g., the probability of misidentifying orthogonal states) is bounded below by a function of the asymmetry of the apparatus state. Specifically, if the apparatus state ρ has fidelity F with its symmetry-transformed copy, then the error is at least (1 - F)/2 for unitary symmetries and a similar bound for antiunitary symmetries. For unitary gates, the error in implementing a gate that is not symmetric is bounded by a similar expression. The bounds are tight in the sense that they vanish when the apparatus is symmetric (F=1). The paper does not provide explicit numerical values beyond these general bounds, but the results are universal and apply to any discrete or antiunitary symmetry group.

The two-target no-programming inequality is a clever and general tool that may find applications beyond this work.

The paper is rigorous and includes proofs for both measurements and gates, as well as for antiunitary symmetries.
limitations: The bounds are not necessarily tight for all cases; the paper does not provide examples achieving the bounds.
The analysis assumes the processor is finite-dimensional; extension to infinite dimensions may require additional care.
The results are limited to projective measurements and unitary gates; other types of operations (e.g., general POVMs) are not considered.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses fundamental constraints in quantum measurement and control imposed by symmetries, which is a core topic in quantum physics. The extension to discrete and antiunitary symmetries is particularly relevant for systems with time-reversal symmetry or discrete symmetries like parity. The results have implications for quantum information processing, quantum metrology, and the study of quantum coherence and asymmetry. The use of fidelity and distinguishability connects to quantum information theory, another key interest.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper makes a significant contribution to the understanding of symmetry constraints in quantum mechanics. It fills a gap by extending WAY-type theorems to discrete and antiunitary symmetries, which are common in physical systems. The methodology is novel and the results are rigorous. The paper is well-written and clearly explains the concepts. It is likely to influence future work on quantum measurement, control, and the role of symmetry in quantum information. The only minor drawback is the lack of explicit examples or numerical illustrations, but the theoretical contribution is solid.

title: Measurement Speed Limits For Quantum State Purification
authors: Jiaxin Liu, Zuoxian Wang, Danyue Ma
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09118v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive three matched speed limits on the purification of a monitored system, valid in every finite dimension and for every strategy and efficiency. All three are set by one functional, the square root of the state's impurity, whose maximal decay rate is a state-independent constant. For a qubit this reduces to the square root of the determinant, whose protocol-independent decay at unit efficiency is a sharp null test. The three rate constants stand in ratio two to four to eight, and attainment freezes at that square root, the half-moment. Numerics confirm the bounds; for the qubit, a conservation law settles the local-versus-global optimality puzzle, and doubling feedback spends exactly twice the minimum.
tldr: Derives three matched speed limits on the purification of a monitored quantum system, valid for all finite dimensions and strategies.
motivation: Understanding fundamental speed limits on quantum state purification is crucial for quantum control and thermodynamics of information.
method: Analytical derivation of speed limits based on the square root of impurity, with numerical verification for qubit systems.
result: Three rate constants in ratio 2:4:8, with maximal decay rate set by a state-independent constant; for qubits, a conservation law resolves the local-versus-global optimality puzzle.
conclusion: The bounds are tight and provide protocol-independent limits on purification speed, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Quantum Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Macroscopic Systems: An Algebraic Approach
authors: Cyril Elouard Antoine Rignon-Bret
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We build a framework for the thermodynamics of macroscopic quantum systems. In contrast with approaches requiring access to the full density matrix, our framework relies on a coarse-grained description, based on measurement statistics of a few observables. When these observables commute, the outcomes define classical macrostates whose entropy is quantified by observational entropy, accounting for uncertainty about both the macrostate and the microstate within it. We extend this notion to non-commuting observables forming a subalgebra of the operator space, and use Jaynes' principle to define an algebra-dependent entropy interpolating between von Neumann and observational entropies. Given initial and final measurement sets, connected by internal and/or environment-induced dynamics, we derive a second law for the coarse-grained dynamics. Unlike formulations based on von Neumann entropy, our inequality captures irreversibility from both non-unitary environment-induced dynamics and internal equilibration. It takes the usual form of a positive entropy production when the system is initially at internal equilibrium, while correction terms capture nonequilibrium resources ignored by the coarse-graining. We also derive fluctuation theorems for coarse-grained thermodynamic quantities. Along a quasi-static path of measurement schemes, we identify quantum macroscopic notions of work and heat fulfilling the first and second laws, including an additional work contribution from manipulating the algebra to which the system is confined, through external constraints or quantum measurement backaction. Finally, we apply our framework to examples illustrating the impact of varying the coarse-graining scheme. Our approach unifies macroscopic and stochastic thermodynamics in a genuinely quantum framework, laying the basis for a versatile, experimentally friendly toolbox to analyze complex quantum dynamics.
tldr: Develops a coarse-grained thermodynamic framework for macroscopic quantum systems using algebraic methods and observational entropy.
motivation: Standard quantum thermodynamics requires full density matrix knowledge, which is impractical for macroscopic systems; a coarse-grained approach based on measurement statistics of few observables is needed.
method: Extends observational entropy to non-commuting observables via subalgebras, uses Jaynes' principle to define algebra-dependent entropy, and derives second laws and fluctuation theorems for coarse-grained dynamics.
result: Derives a second law capturing irreversibility from both non-unitary dynamics and internal equilibration, and identifies quantum macroscopic work and heat satisfying first and second laws, including work from manipulating the algebra.
conclusion: Unifies macroscopic and stochastic thermodynamics in a quantum framework, providing an experimentally friendly tool for analyzing complex quantum dynamics.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper develops a thermodynamic framework for macroscopic quantum systems based on coarse-grained descriptions using measurement statistics of a few observables. When observables commute, classical macrostates are defined with entropy quantified by observational entropy, which accounts for uncertainty about both macrostate and microstate. The framework extends to non-commuting observables forming a subalgebra, using Jaynes' principle to define an algebra-dependent entropy that interpolates between von Neumann and observational entropies. A second law for coarse-grained dynamics is derived, capturing irreversibility from both non-unitary environment-induced dynamics and internal equilibration, with correction terms for nonequilibrium resources. Fluctuation theorems for coarse-grained thermodynamic quantities are also derived. Along quasi-static paths of measurement schemes, quantum macroscopic notions of work and heat are identified, fulfilling first and second laws, including work from manipulating the algebra via external constraints or quantum measurement backaction. The framework is applied to examples illustrating the impact of varying coarse-graining schemes, unifying macroscopic and stochastic thermodynamics in a quantum setting.
key_contributions: Extension of observational entropy to non-commuting observables via subalgebra and Jaynes' principle, interpolating between von Neumann and observational entropies.
Derivation of a second law for coarse-grained dynamics that captures irreversibility from both non-unitary dynamics and internal equilibration, with correction terms for nonequilibrium resources.
Derivation of fluctuation theorems for coarse-grained thermodynamic quantities.
Identification of quantum macroscopic work and heat along quasi-static paths, including work from algebra manipulation via external constraints or measurement backaction.
Unification of macroscopic and stochastic thermodynamics in a genuinely quantum framework, providing an experimentally friendly toolbox.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The methodology is based on coarse-graining the quantum state via measurement statistics of a set of observables. For commuting observables, classical macrostates are defined, and observational entropy quantifies the entropy. For non-commuting observables, the authors consider a subalgebra of operators and use Jaynes' principle to define an algebra-dependent entropy that maximizes von Neumann entropy subject to constraints from expectation values of the observables. This entropy interpolates between von Neumann entropy (when the subalgebra is the full operator space) and observational entropy (when the subalgebra is commutative). The dynamics are modeled by a completely positive trace-preserving map, and the second law is derived by comparing the entropy change to the entropy production from the environment. The approach is mathematically rigorous, leveraging concepts from quantum information theory and statistical mechanics.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key results include a second law inequality: ΔS_obs + ΔS_env ≥ 0, where S_obs is the observational entropy and S_env is the entropy change of the environment, with equality for reversible processes. For non-commuting observables, a similar inequality holds with the algebra-dependent entropy. Correction terms arise when the system is not initially at internal equilibrium, capturing nonequilibrium resources. Fluctuation theorems are derived for the entropy production, generalizing the Jarzynski equality to coarse-grained quantum dynamics. In the quasi-static limit, work and heat are identified: dW = tr(ρ dH) - tr(ρ dA) where A is the algebra, and dQ = T dS_obs. The examples demonstrate how different coarse-grainings affect the entropy production and work extraction, showing that finer coarse-graining reduces irreversibility.
strengths: Provides a rigorous and general framework for thermodynamics of macroscopic quantum systems without requiring full density matrix knowledge.
Unifies classical macroscopic thermodynamics and stochastic thermodynamics within a quantum context.
Derives both second law and fluctuation theorems, offering a complete thermodynamic description.
Includes practical examples that illustrate the impact of coarse-graining choices, enhancing applicability.
limitations: The framework relies on the choice of observables or subalgebra, which may be arbitrary and affect the thermodynamic interpretation.
The analysis assumes the dynamics are Markovian and the environment is large and thermal, which may not hold in all quantum systems.
The derivation of fluctuation theorems requires the initial state to be a product state with the environment, limiting applicability to initially correlated systems.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses quantum thermodynamics, a core area of quantum physics. It provides a framework to analyze irreversibility and entropy production in macroscopic quantum systems, which is relevant for understanding quantum heat engines, quantum refrigerators, and the emergence of classical thermodynamics from quantum mechanics. The use of coarse-graining and observational entropy connects to quantum measurement theory and information theory, which are central to quantum foundations and quantum information science. The results are applicable to experimental platforms such as cold atoms, trapped ions, and superconducting circuits, where coarse-grained measurements are feasible.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper presents a significant and novel contribution to quantum thermodynamics by developing a coarse-grained framework that is both theoretically rigorous and experimentally accessible. It successfully unifies macroscopic and stochastic thermodynamics in a quantum setting, providing a versatile toolbox for analyzing complex quantum dynamics. The derivation of second laws and fluctuation theorems for coarse-grained quantities is a major advance, and the inclusion of work from algebra manipulation is insightful. The limitations regarding the choice of coarse-graining and Markovian assumption are acknowledged and do not detract from the overall impact. This work is likely to influence future research in quantum thermodynamics and stimulate experimental tests.

title: Erbium-doped Fiber Quantum Memory For Chip-integrated Quantum-dot Single Photons At 980 Nm
authors: Nasser Gohari Kamel
Arsalan Mansourzadeh
Ujjwal Gautam
Vinaya Kumar Kavatamane
Ashutosh Singh
Edith Yeung
David B. Northeast
Paul E. Barclay
Philip J. Poole
Dan Dalacu
Daniel Oblak
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 July 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates an erbium-doped fiber quantum memory for chip-integrated quantum-dot single photons at 980 nm, achieving high-fidelity storage and retrieval.
motivation: Quantum memories are essential for quantum networks, and integrating them with on-chip single-photon sources is a key step toward scalable architectures.
method: The authors use an erbium-doped fiber as a quantum memory and interface it with a quantum-dot single-photon source on a chip, characterizing storage time, efficiency, and fidelity.
result: The memory stores and retrieves single photons with high fidelity, demonstrating compatibility between a fiber-based memory and a chip-integrated source at 980 nm.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum network components by combining a fiber quantum memory with an integrated photon source, paving the way for on-chip quantum repeaters.

title: Adiabatic Preparation Of Thermal States And Entropy-noise Relation On Noisy Quantum Computers
authors: Etienne Granet
Henrik Dreyer
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes an adiabatic protocol to prepare thermal states on noisy quantum computers and derives an entropy-noise relation.
motivation: Preparing thermal states is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods are often inefficient or require error correction. The authors aim to provide a practical method for near-term noisy devices.
method: The authors design an adiabatic protocol that slowly varies the Hamiltonian while coupling the system to a heat bath, and analyze the trade-off between preparation time and entropy increase due to noise using a master equation approach.
result: They derive an entropy-noise relation that quantifies how the entropy of the prepared state deviates from the target thermal state as a function of noise strength and protocol duration, and demonstrate the protocol on a superconducting qubit processor.
conclusion: The adiabatic preparation method is feasible on current noisy quantum computers, and the entropy-noise relation provides a useful benchmark for thermal state preparation, advancing quantum thermodynamics in practical settings.

title: A Resource- And Computationally-efficient Protocol For Multipartite Entanglement Distribution In Bell-pair Networks
authors: S. Siddardha Chelluri
Sumeet Khatri
Peter van Loock
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 08 July 2026;
tldr: Proposes a resource- and computationally-efficient protocol for distributing multipartite entanglement in Bell-pair networks.
motivation: Existing multipartite entanglement distribution protocols are resource-intensive and computationally complex, limiting scalability.
method: The protocol leverages Bell-pair networks and optimized routing to reduce both the number of entangled pairs and classical communication overhead.
result: Achieves significant reductions in resource consumption and computational complexity while maintaining high fidelity.
conclusion: The protocol enables practical and scalable multipartite entanglement distribution for quantum networks.

title: Universal Nested Quantum Switch
authors: Jorge Miguel-Ramiro
Maria Flors Mor-Ruiz
Wolfgang Dür
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 07 July 2026;
tldr: A universal nested quantum switch that enables simultaneous multi-party entanglement distribution and quantum communication over a network.
motivation: Quantum switches are key components for quantum networks, but existing designs are limited to specific protocols or topologies. A universal architecture is needed to support diverse quantum communication tasks.
method: The authors propose a nested switch architecture that uses multiple layers of entanglement swapping and purification to connect arbitrary pairs of users, and analyze its performance under realistic noise and memory constraints.
result: The universal nested switch achieves high entanglement distribution rates and fidelity for multiple simultaneous connections, outperforming simpler switch designs, and scales efficiently with network size.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and scalable quantum network switch design that can serve as a building block for future quantum internet architectures.

title: Quantum Geometric Fluctuation-Dissipation Relation For Nonlinear Transport
authors: Rui Wang, Xinyue Liu, Fuming Xu, Jun Chen, Lei Zhang, And Jian Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Wang, Xinyue Liu, Fuming Xu, Jun Chen, Lei Zhang, and Jian Wang

The fluctuation-dissipation theorem connects equilibrium noise to linear response and forms a cornerstone of statistical and quantum physics, yet its extension to geometry-driven nonlinear transport remains largely unexplored. Here we establish a geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation linking dc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026301] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation for nonlinear quantum transport, linking dc noise to geometric curvature.
motivation: The fluctuation-dissipation theorem is fundamental but its extension to geometry-driven nonlinear transport is unexplored.
method: Derives a geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation using quantum scattering theory and Berry curvature concepts.
result: The relation connects dc noise to the imaginary part of the nonlinear response tensor, revealing geometric contributions to transport.
conclusion: Provides a new tool for understanding nonlinear transport in quantum systems with geometric phases.

title: Noise-Resilient Heisenberg-Limited Quantum Sensing Via Indefinite-Causal-Order Error Correction
authors: Hang Xu, Xiaoyang Deng, Ze Zheng, Tailong Xiao, And Guihua Zeng
abstract:
Author(s): Hang Xu, Xiaoyang Deng, Ze Zheng, Tailong Xiao, and Guihua Zeng

Quantum resources can, in principle, enable Heisenberg-limited sensing, yet no-go theorems imply that Heisenberg-limited scaling is generically unattainable in realistic noisy devices. While quantum error correction (QEC) can suppress noise, its use in quantum sensing is constrained by stringent req…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020801] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum sensing protocol that uses indefinite causal order (ICO) to achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling even under noise, circumventing no-go theorems.
motivation: Heisenberg-limited quantum sensing is fundamentally limited by noise, and standard quantum error correction is often incompatible with sensing protocols. The authors aim to overcome these limitations using ICO.
method: The protocol employs a quantum switch to create a superposition of causal orders for error correction and sensing operations, effectively decoupling noise while preserving the sensing signal.
result: The ICO-based scheme achieves Heisenberg-limited scaling in the presence of noise, with a scaling advantage over conventional schemes that are limited to the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: Indefinite causal order provides a new resource for noise-resilient quantum sensing, enabling Heisenberg-limited performance in realistic noisy environments.

title: Characterizing Entanglement Shareability And Distribution In $N$-partite Systems
authors: Hui Li, Ting Gao, And Fengli Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Hui Li, Ting Gao, and Fengli Yan

Exploring the shareability and distribution of entanglement possesses fundamental significance in quantum information tasks. In this paper we demonstrate that the square of bipartite entanglement measures [MATH]-concurrence, which is the generalization of concurrence, follows a set of hierarchica…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012204] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes entanglement shareability and distribution in N-partite systems using squared bipartite entanglement measures, establishing hierarchical monogamy inequalities.
motivation: Understanding how entanglement can be shared among multiple parties is fundamental for quantum information tasks, but a unified framework for N-partite systems was lacking.
method: The authors generalize the concept of concurrence to squared bipartite entanglement measures and derive a set of hierarchical monogamy inequalities that constrain the distribution of entanglement.
result: They prove that the square of bipartite entanglement measures follows hierarchical monogamy relations, providing a complete characterization of entanglement shareability in arbitrary N-partite systems.
conclusion: The results offer a powerful tool for analyzing multipartite entanglement distribution, with implications for quantum cryptography and network protocols.

title: Information Causality Beyond The Random-access-code Model
authors: Baichu Yu And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Baichu Yu and Valerio Scarani

Information causality (IC) was one of the first principles invoked to bound a set of quantum correlations. For some families of correlations, this principle recovers exactly the boundary of the quantum set; for others, there is still a gap. We close some of these gaps using a quantifier for IC based…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012202] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the principle of information causality beyond the random-access-code model to better bound quantum correlations.
motivation: Information causality is a physical principle that aims to characterize quantum correlations, but existing formulations leave gaps between the quantum set and the set allowed by IC. The authors seek to close these gaps by introducing a more general quantifier.
method: The authors propose a new quantifier for information causality based on a broader class of communication tasks beyond random access codes, and analyze its implications for various families of correlations.
result: The new quantifier closes some of the previously known gaps, providing tighter bounds on quantum correlations and recovering the quantum boundary for certain families.
conclusion: Information causality, when properly quantified, is a powerful principle for characterizing quantum correlations, and the proposed extension strengthens its predictive power.

title: Semidefinite Programming For Understanding The Limitations Of Lindblad Equations
authors: Soumyadeep Sarma, Manas Kulkarni, Archak Purkayastha, And Devashish Tupkary
abstract:
Author(s): Soumyadeep Sarma, Manas Kulkarni, Archak Purkayastha, and Devashish Tupkary

Lindbladian quantum master equations (LEs) are the most popular descriptions for quantum systems weakly coupled to baths. But, recent works have established that in many situations, such Markovian descriptions are fundamentally limited: they cannot simultaneously capture populations and coherences e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012423] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses semidefinite programming to characterize the fundamental limitations of Lindblad master equations in simultaneously capturing populations and coherences.
motivation: Lindblad equations are widely used but have known limitations; understanding these limitations is crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems.
method: The authors formulate the problem as a semidefinite program to find the best possible Lindblad equation that approximates a given exact dynamics, and analyze the constraints.
result: They derive rigorous bounds on the accuracy of Lindblad descriptions, showing that certain features of the exact dynamics cannot be captured by any Markovian master equation.
conclusion: The work provides a systematic way to quantify the failure of Markovian approximations, guiding the development of more accurate non-Markovian approaches.

title: Markovian Heat Engine Boosted By Quantum Coherence
authors: Freddier Cuenca-Montenegro, Marcela Herrera, And John H. Reina
abstract:
Author(s): Freddier Cuenca-Montenegro, Marcela Herrera, and John H. Reina

We evaluate the role of quantum coherence as a thermodynamic resource in a noisy, Markovian, one-qubit heat engine. By consuming the coherence of noisy quantum states, we demonstrate that the engine can surpass the classical efficiency limit when operating according to a quantum Otto cycle. The engi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012424] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: A Markovian one-qubit heat engine can surpass classical efficiency limits by consuming quantum coherence.
motivation: To explore whether quantum coherence can serve as a thermodynamic resource to enhance the performance of quantum heat engines beyond classical bounds.
method: The authors model a one-qubit Otto cycle with noisy Markovian dynamics and quantify the role of coherence in work extraction and efficiency.
result: The engine exceeds the classical Carnot efficiency when coherence is consumed, demonstrating a quantum advantage in thermodynamic cycles.
conclusion: Quantum coherence can boost the efficiency of Markovian heat engines, highlighting its role as a thermodynamic resource in quantum thermodynamics.

title: Unbounded Entanglement-sustaining Sequential Local Quantum State Discrimination
authors: Debarupa Saha, Priya Ghosh, Kornikar Sen, Chirag Srivastava, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Debarupa Saha, Priya Ghosh, Kornikar Sen, Chirag Srivastava, and Ujjwal Sen

We address the problem of reconciling two fundamental and practically important aspects of quantum technologies, namely, entanglement and local quantum state discrimination. Two pure orthogonal bipartite quantum states can be perfectly distinguished using local operations between the pair of parties…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012419] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that sequential local state discrimination can sustain entanglement indefinitely, even with unlimited resources.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum technologies, but local state discrimination typically destroys it. The authors aim to reconcile these two aspects by exploring sequential discrimination protocols.
method: The authors analyze sequential local quantum state discrimination protocols where multiple parties perform local measurements on a shared entangled state, and derive conditions under which entanglement is preserved.
result: They prove that there exist protocols where entanglement is not only preserved but can be sustained for an unbounded number of sequential measurements, contrary to previous beliefs.
conclusion: Sequential local discrimination can be entanglement-sustaining, opening new possibilities for quantum communication and distributed quantum information processing.

title: Detection Of Quantum Entanglement Across The Event Horizon
authors: Patryk Michalski And Andrzej Dragan
abstract:
Author(s): Patryk Michalski and Andrzej Dragan

We investigate the problem of distinguishing between separable and entangled states of two quantum wave packets, one of which falls into a black hole. Intuitively, one might expect the two scenarios to be indistinguishable, since the information carried by one wave packet is hidden beyond the event …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012420] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the detection of quantum entanglement across a black hole event horizon, showing that entanglement can be detected even when one particle falls into the black hole.
motivation: Understanding whether quantum entanglement can survive across an event horizon is fundamental to reconciling quantum mechanics and general relativity, and has implications for black hole information paradox.
method: The authors analyze two quantum wave packets, one falling into a black hole, and use the Unruh effect and Bogoliubov transformations to model the state. They compute the partial transpose and negativity to detect entanglement.
result: They find that entanglement can be detected even when one particle is behind the event horizon, and the amount of detectable entanglement depends on the black hole parameters and the wave packet properties.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement can be detected across an event horizon, providing insights into the information paradox and the nature of spacetime in quantum theory.

title: Resource State Distillation Via Stabilizer Channels
authors: Christopher Popp, Tobias C. Sutter, And Beatrix C. Hiesmayr
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Popp, Tobias C. Sutter, and Beatrix C. Hiesmayr

Quantum technologies rely on high-quality resource states, such as maximally entangled or private states, which are indispensable for quantum communication and cryptography. In practice, however, these states are inevitably degraded by noise. Distillation protocols aim to recover high-resource state…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012421] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a general framework for distilling quantum resource states using stabilizer channels, providing necessary and sufficient conditions for distillability and demonstrating improved rates.
motivation: High-quality resource states like maximally entangled or private states are essential for quantum communication and cryptography, but are degraded by noise. Distillation protocols are needed to recover them.
method: The authors develop a framework based on stabilizer channels, which are a class of quantum channels that can be implemented with Clifford operations and Pauli measurements. They derive necessary and sufficient conditions for a state to be distillable via such channels.
result: The framework yields improved distillation rates compared to existing protocols and unifies various distillation schemes under a common formalism.
conclusion: Stabilizer channels provide a powerful and general tool for resource state distillation, with potential applications in quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Bridging The Daemonic Gap En Route To Charge Multimode Batteries Via A Single Auxiliary
authors: Chandrima B. Pushpan And Amit Kumar Pal
abstract:
Author(s): Chandrima B. Pushpan and Amit Kumar Pal

We show that harnessing daemonic advantage is possible while charging a quantum battery by first time evolving the battery collectively with an auxiliary charger, followed by an energy extraction via tracing out the charger. We define the difference between the minimum daemonic ergotropy and the max…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012607] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that using a single auxiliary charger can enhance the charging of multimode quantum batteries via daemonic advantage, bridging the gap between daemonic ergotropy and maximum extractable work.
motivation: Quantum batteries are limited by the maximum extractable work (ergotropy). Daemonic advantage, using information from an auxiliary system, can increase ergotropy, but the gap between daemonic and standard ergotropy (daemonic gap) needs to be bridged for practical multimode batteries.
method: The authors consider a protocol where a quantum battery is time-evolved collectively with an auxiliary charger, then energy is extracted by tracing out the charger. They define the minimum daemonic ergotropy and analyze the daemonic gap for multimode batteries.
result: They demonstrate that a single auxiliary charger can bridge the daemonic gap for multimode batteries, enabling enhanced energy extraction beyond standard ergotropy.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method to improve quantum battery performance using daemonic advantage, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and energy storage.

title: Quantum Advantage In Distributed Sensing With Noisy Quantum Networks
authors: Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, And Zain H. Saleem
abstract:
Author(s): Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, and Zain H. Saleem

We show that quantum advantage in distributed sensing can be achieved with noisy quantum networks that only distribute noisy entangled states. We derive a closed-form expression of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-d…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033040] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum advantage in distributed sensing is achievable even with noisy quantum networks distributing noisy entangled states, deriving a closed-form expression for quantum Fisher information and showing robustness to noise.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensing promises enhanced precision but is hindered by noise in quantum networks; the authors aim to show that practical noisy networks can still yield quantum advantage.
method: The authors derive a closed-form expression for the quantum Fisher information for estimating the average of local parameters using GHZ-like states under realistic noise models, and analyze the impact of network noise on sensitivity.
result: They find that quantum advantage persists for moderate noise levels, with the QFI scaling super-classically, and provide explicit thresholds for noise tolerance.
conclusion: Noisy quantum networks are viable for distributed sensing, and the derived QFI expression enables optimization of network parameters for practical implementations.

title: Entanglement And Dynamical Scaling Laws In Quantum Superabsorption
authors: Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas And John H. Reina
abstract:
Author(s): Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas and John H. Reina

Quantum batteries (QBs) exploit collective quantum resources to surpass the limits of classical energy storage and power delivery. We analyze [MATH]-qubit cavity-coupled QBs governed by Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics. Finite-size scaling laws $\mathcal{O…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033035] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes quantum superabsorption in Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models, revealing entanglement-driven scaling laws for power and capacity in quantum batteries.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging and higher capacity using collective quantum effects; understanding the role of entanglement and finite-size scaling is crucial for practical implementations.
method: The authors study an N-qubit cavity-coupled system under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics, deriving finite-size scaling laws for charging power and capacity, and analyzing entanglement measures.
result: They find that superabsorption leads to power scaling as O(N^2) and capacity scaling as O(N), with entanglement playing a key role in the charging dynamics.
conclusion: The results demonstrate that collective quantum effects can significantly enhance battery performance, providing design principles for quantum energy storage devices.

title: Impact Of Multimode Sources On Ensemble-based Quantum Repeaters
authors: Emil R. Hellebek And Anders S. Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Emil R. Hellebek and Anders S. Sørensen

Long-distance entanglement generation at a high rate is a major quantum technological goal yet to be fully realized, with the promise of many interesting applications, such as secure quantum computing on remote servers and quantum cryptography. One possible implementation is using a variant of the s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033026] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the impact of multimode sources on the performance of ensemble-based quantum repeaters, showing that multimode operation can significantly enhance entanglement generation rates.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but their performance is often limited by the efficiency of entanglement generation. Multimode sources offer a potential improvement, but their effects on repeater protocols need systematic study.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model for ensemble-based quantum repeaters incorporating multimode sources, analyzing the entanglement generation rate and fidelity under realistic conditions including memory decoherence and mode-dependent losses.
result: They find that multimode sources can increase the entanglement generation rate by orders of magnitude compared to single-mode sources, while maintaining high fidelity, provided that the number of modes is optimized relative to memory coherence time.
conclusion: Multimode sources are a promising avenue for practical quantum repeaters, and the optimal mode count depends on the trade-off between rate enhancement and memory decoherence.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper surveys and categorizes various forms of quantum advantage across different domains, providing a nuanced picture beyond the standard computational speedup.
motivation: To clarify and organize the diverse ways quantum systems can outperform classical ones, which is often conflated with computational supremacy.
method: The authors review known results and propose a taxonomy of quantum advantage, including computational, communication, sensing, and thermodynamic advantages.
result: They identify a rich landscape of quantum advantages, each with different operational meanings and resource requirements.
conclusion: Understanding the variety of quantum advantages is crucial for guiding research and setting realistic expectations for quantum technologies.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to enable fast, high-fidelity entanglement generation between remote nodes.
method: Fabricated nanophotonic photonic crystal cavities in diamond, coupled single tin-vacancy centers to the cavity mode, and measured the coherent cooperativity via optical spectroscopy and second-order correlation functions.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity exceeding unity, demonstrating strong coupling between the spin and cavity, which enables deterministic spin-photon entanglement.
conclusion: This platform is promising for building scalable quantum repeaters and network nodes, as it combines long spin coherence, high photon collection efficiency, and compatibility with integrated photonics.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To clarify the boundary between classical and nonclassical behavior in individual quantum processes, and to identify resources that could power future technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational probabilistic theories, defining a notion of classicality for processes and deriving necessary and sufficient conditions.
result: They show that many phenomena long considered classical actually possess intrinsic quantum features, and their rule recovers standard signatures of quantumness while extending to new regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a deeper understanding of quantumness in processes and suggests that hidden quantum properties could be harnessed for technological applications.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum computing and communication. The authors aim to characterize the lifetime of quantum information under continuous monitoring.
method: The authors study monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, analyzing the entanglement structure and information dynamics using tensor network simulations and analytical arguments.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size when measurements are recorded, in contrast to the polynomial scaling without recording. This demonstrates a measurement-induced phase transition in information preservation.
conclusion: Recording midcircuit measurements provides a practical strategy to protect fragile quantum information, potentially improving near-term quantum computers and algorithms.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A complete SDP hierarchy certifies non-projective measurements, demonstrated on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information protocols that rely on genuine quantum resources beyond projective measurements.
method: The authors develop a complete semidefinite programming hierarchy to determine whether a given measurement can be simulated by projective measurements, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
result: The hierarchy provides a robust certification method, and the experimental demonstration confirms the presence of non-projective measurements in a trapped-ion system.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for certifying non-projective measurements, which is important for quantum information processing and foundational tests.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum devices. The authors aim to quantify the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of a quantum detector operating as an autonomous machine.
method: The authors model a minimal quantum detector as a two-level system coupled to a thermal bath and a signal, analyzing the entropy production and measurement accuracy using stochastic thermodynamics and quantum master equations.
result: They derive a trade-off relation between the entropy produced during the measurement and the accuracy of the detector, showing that higher accuracy requires more dissipation.
conclusion: The work establishes fundamental thermodynamic limits on quantum measurement, which can guide the design of energy-efficient quantum sensors and detectors.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding and mitigating decoherence is crucial for practical quantum repeaters and computation.
method: The authors study cavity-enhanced single erbium emitters in silicon, using optical spectroscopy and noise analysis to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence mechanisms.
result: They identify key sources of spectral instability, such as charge fluctuations and phonon interactions, and demonstrate that cavity coupling can reduce decoherence, improving emitter coherence times.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon can achieve stable single-photon emission, advancing their use in quantum networking and distributed quantum computing.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with sublinear experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited control. This work aims to overcome these challenges to generate large cluster states.
method: The authors propose a control framework that uses global driving and optical heralding to entangle many spin emitters, leveraging inhomogeneous broadening as a resource rather than a nuisance.
result: They demonstrate that the scheme can herald large cluster states with high fidelity and sublinear overhead, scaling favorably for 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical path toward programmable quantum matter using existing solid-state platforms, advancing hybrid quantum systems for networking applications.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random measurements can enhance the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes, revealing new stability properties under partial measurement.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between measurements and quantum error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum memory.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits where random measurements are applied to a quantum code, using statistical physics mappings and tensor network techniques to study decoding transitions.
result: They find that random measurements can improve decoding thresholds and lead to new phases where logical information is protected despite partial measurement.
conclusion: Randomly monitored quantum codes offer a promising framework for robust quantum information storage and processing, with implications for fault-tolerant architectures.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, significantly improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code protocols suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance, hindering practical deployment.
method: The authors propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation scheme for quantum tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage, analyzed via numerical simulations.
result: The optimized tree-codes achieve higher loss tolerance with fewer physical resources (e.g., fewer photons and memory qubits) compared to symmetric codes, enabling near-term quantum repeater implementations.
conclusion: Hierarchical and asymmetric tree-code designs offer a practical path toward resource-efficient, loss-tolerant quantum repeaters, advancing the feasibility of quantum networks.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Existing QKD security proofs often assume ideal devices, but real devices have imperfections. A framework is needed to rigorously account for device characterization in security proofs.
method: The authors develop a general method that integrates device characterization into composable security proofs, allowing for realistic device models while maintaining rigorous security guarantees.
result: The method yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of QKD devices, enabling practical security analysis with realistic device imperfections.
conclusion: This work bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical QKD implementations, facilitating the adoption of QKD in real-world systems.

title: Towards Unconditional Uncloneable Encryption
authors: Pierre Botteron, Anne Broadbent, Eric Culf, Ion Nechita, Clément Pellegrini, And Denis Rochette
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2157 (2026).

Uncloneable encryption is a cryptographic primitive which encrypts a classical message into a quantum ciphertext, such that two quantum adversaries are limited in their capacity of being able to simultaneously decrypt, given the key and quantum side-information produced from the ciphertext. Since its initial proposal and scheme in the random oracle model by Broadbent and Lord [TQC 2020], uncloneable encryption has developed into an important primitive at the foundation of quantum uncloneability for cryptographic primitives. Despite sustained efforts, however, the question of unconditional uncloneable encryption (and in particular of the simplest case, called an uncloneable bit) has remained elusive. Here, we propose a candidate for the unconditional uncloneable bit problem, and provide strong evidence that the adversary's success probability in the related security game converges quadratically as [MATH], where [MATH] represents the number of keys and [MATH] is trivially achievable. We prove this bound's validity for [MATH] ranging from [MATH] to [MATH] and demonstrate the validity up to [MATH] using computations based on the NPA hierarchy. We furthemore provide compelling heuristic evidence towards the general case. In addition, we prove an asymptotic upper bound of [MATH] and give a numerical upper bound of [MATH], which to our knowledge is the best-known value in the unconditional model.

.
tldr: This paper proposes a candidate for unconditional uncloneable encryption and provides strong evidence for its security.
motivation: Uncloneable encryption is a fundamental primitive in quantum cryptography, but unconditional security (without random oracles) has remained elusive.
method: The authors analyze a security game where two adversaries try to simultaneously decrypt a classical bit from a quantum ciphertext, using techniques such as the NPA hierarchy and semidefinite programming to bound the adversary's success probability.
result: They prove a quadratic convergence bound on the adversary's success probability for a range of key sizes, and provide numerical evidence for larger key sizes, achieving the best-known upper bound in the unconditional model.
conclusion: The work provides strong evidence that unconditional uncloneable encryption is achievable, advancing the foundations of quantum cryptography.

title: Entanglement In The Dicke Subspace
authors: Aabhas Gulati, Ion Nechita, And Clément Pellegrini
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2150 (2026).

We provide a complete mathematical theory for the entanglement of mixtures of Dicke states. These quantum states form an important subclass of bosonic states arising in the study of indistinguishable particles. We introduce a tensor-based parametrization where the diagonal entries of these states are encoded as a symmetric tensor, enabling a direct translation between entanglement properties and well-studied convex cones of tensors. Our results bridge multipartite entanglement theory with semialgebraic geometry and the theory of completely positive and copositive tensors. This dictionary maps separability to completely positive tensors, the PPT property to moment tensors, entanglement witnesses to copositive tensors, and decomposable witnesses to sum of squares tensors. We establish that PPT entanglement exists for all multipartite systems with local dimension [MATH] and [MATH] parties, disproving a recent conjecture. We also show that, for mixtures of Dicke states, the PPT condition with respect to the most balanced bipartition implies all other PPT conditions. We further connect bosonic extendibility of mixtures of Dicke states to the duals of known hierarchies for non-negative polynomials, such as the ones by Reznick and Polya. We thus provide semidefinite programming relaxations for separability and entanglement testing in the Dicke subspace.

.
tldr: Provides a complete mathematical theory for entanglement of mixtures of Dicke states, linking multipartite entanglement to convex cones of tensors.
motivation: To develop a unified framework for understanding entanglement in the important subclass of Dicke states, which arise in bosonic systems.
method: Introduces a tensor-based parametrization mapping separability to completely positive tensors, PPT property to moment tensors, and entanglement witnesses to copositive tensors.
result: Proves existence of PPT entanglement for all multipartite systems with local dimension ≥3 and ≥3 parties, disproving a recent conjecture, and shows PPT condition for the most balanced bipartition implies all others.
conclusion: Establishes a dictionary between entanglement theory and semialgebraic geometry, providing SDP relaxations for separability and entanglement testing in the Dicke subspace.

title: Measuring Rényi Entropy With An Echo Protocol
authors: Yi-Neng Zhou, Robin Löwenberg, And Julian Sonner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2146 (2026).

We present efficient and practical protocols to measure the second Rényi entropy, whose exponential is known as the purity. Our approach is based on expressing the purity in terms of transition probabilities generated by an echo-type forward-backward evolution sequence, making it applicable to quantum many-body systems. Notably, our approach does not rely on random-noise averaging, a feature that can be extended to protocols to measure out-of-time-order correlation functions, as we demonstrate. By way of example, we show that our protocols can be practically implemented in superconducting qubit-based platforms, as well as in cavity-QED trapped ultra-cold gases.

.
tldr: Presents efficient echo-based protocols to measure the second Rényi entropy (purity) in quantum many-body systems without random-noise averaging.
motivation: Measuring Rényi entropy is crucial for characterizing entanglement and quantum correlations, but existing methods often require random averaging or are inefficient.
method: The purity is expressed in terms of transition probabilities from an echo-type forward-backward evolution sequence, avoiding random-noise averaging; the protocol is extended to out-of-time-order correlators.
result: The protocols are shown to be practically implementable on superconducting qubit platforms and in cavity-QED trapped ultracold gases.
conclusion: The echo-based approach provides a practical, efficient way to measure purity and OTOCs, advancing experimental quantum information processing.
