title: Decoupling Local Classicality From Classical Explainability: A Noncontextual Model For Bilocal Classical Theory And A Locally-classical But Contextual Theory
authors: Sina Soltani, Marco Erba, David Schmid, And John H.selby
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2142 (2026).

We construct an ontological model for the theory known as bilocal classical theory [1]. To our knowledge, this is only the second time that an ontological model has been constructed for an entire theory, rather than just for some particular scenarios within a theory. This result refutes a conjecture from [1] which suggested that there might be no local-realist ontological model for bilocal classical theory. Moreover, it is the first time that an ontological model has been constructed for a theory that fails to be locally tomographic, showing that the assumption of local tomography underpinning the structure theorem in [2] is a genuine limitation of the theorem. This demonstrates that in general there is no tension between failures of local tomography and classical explainability (i.e., generalised noncontextuality). In fact, bilocal classical theory is in many ways more simply understood via the underlying ontological model than it is within its original formulation (much as how odd-dimensional stabiliser subtheories can be more simply understood via Spekkens' toy theory). Furthermore, this result naturally leads to the question, does every locally-classical theory admit of an ontological model? By constructing a concrete counterexample, we show that this is not the case. Our findings demonstrate that there is no straightforward relationship between theories being locally-classical, and them being classically-explainable. This shows that the fundamental status of compositional properties (such as local tomography) is not a technical side-issue, but a central and unavoidable question for a coherent understanding even of classicality itself.

.
tldr: Constructs an ontological model for bilocal classical theory, refuting a conjecture and showing that local classicality does not imply classical explainability.
motivation: To understand the relationship between local tomography, local classicality, and generalized noncontextuality, and to test whether every locally-classical theory admits an ontological model.
method: Constructs an explicit ontological model for bilocal classical theory using a generalized noncontextual framework, and then builds a counterexample theory that is locally-classical but contextual.
result: Bilocal classical theory has a local-realist ontological model, contrary to a previous conjecture; however, there exist locally-classical theories that are contextual, decoupling local classicality from classical explainability.
conclusion: Compositional properties like local tomography are central to understanding classicality, and the relationship between local classicality and noncontextuality is nontrivial.

title: Measurement Incompatibility And Quantum Steering Via Linear Programming
authors: Lucas E. A. Porto, Sébastien Designolle, Sebastian Pokutta, And Marco Túlio Quintino
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2141 (2026).

The problem of deciding whether a set of quantum measurements is jointly measurable is known to be equivalent to determining whether a quantum assemblage is unsteerable. This problem can be formulated as a semidefinite program (SDP). However, the number of variables and constraints in such a formulation grows exponentially with the number of measurements, rendering it intractable for large measurement sets. In this work, we circumvent this problem by transforming the SDP into a hierarchy of linear programs that compute upper and lower bounds on the incompatibility robustness with a complexity that grows polynomially in the number of measurements. The hierarchy is guaranteed to converge and it can be applied to arbitrary measurements – including non-projective POVMs (Positive Operator-Valued Measures) – in arbitrary dimensions. While convergence becomes impractical in high dimensions, in the case of qubits our method reliably provides accurate upper and lower bounds for the incompatibility robustness of sets with several hundred measurements in a short time using a standard laptop. We also apply our methods to qutrits, obtaining non-trivial upper and lower bounds in scenarios that are otherwise intractable using the standard SDP approach, although such bounds are significantly looser than the ones obtained in the qubit case. Finally, we show how our methods can be used to construct local hidden state models for states (i.e., to prove that a state cannot lead to steering under any possible local measurements), or conversely, to certify that a given state exhibits steering; for two-qubit quantum states, our approach is comparable to, and in some cases outperforms, the current best methods.

.
tldr: This paper transforms the SDP for joint measurability and steering into a hierarchy of linear programs that scales polynomially, enabling efficient computation for large measurement sets.
motivation: The standard SDP for deciding joint measurability and steering becomes intractable for large measurement sets due to exponential growth in variables and constraints.
method: The authors reformulate the SDP as a hierarchy of linear programs that provide upper and lower bounds on incompatibility robustness, with polynomial complexity in the number of measurements.
result: For qubits, the method reliably handles hundreds of measurements on a standard laptop; for qutrits, it provides non-trivial bounds where SDP is intractable. The approach also constructs local hidden state models for steering.
conclusion: The linear programming hierarchy offers a practical tool for analyzing measurement incompatibility and quantum steering in large scenarios, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Tight Bounds For Quantum Phase Estimation And Related Problems
authors: Nikhil S. Mande And Ronald de Wolf
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2140 (2026).

Phase estimation, due to Kitaev [17], is one of the most fundamental subroutines in quantum computing. In the basic scenario, one is given black-box access to a unitary [MATH], and an eigenstate [MATH] of [MATH] with unknown eigenvalue [MATH], and the task is to estimate the eigenphase [MATH] within [MATH], with high probability. The cost of an algorithm for us is the number of applications of [MATH] and [MATH]. We tightly characterize the cost of several variants of phase estimation where we are no longer given an eigenstate, but are required to estimate the maximum eigenphase of [MATH], aided by advice in the form of states (or a unitary preparing those states) which are promised to have at least a certain overlap [MATH] with the top eigenspace. We give algorithms and nearly matching lower bounds for all ranges of parameters. We show that a small number of copies of the advice state (or of an advice-preparing unitary) are not significantly better than having no advice at all. We also show that having lots of advice (applications of the advice-preparing unitary) does not significantly reduce cost, and neither does knowledge of the eigenbasis of [MATH]. We immediately obtain a lower bound on the complexity of the Unitary recurrence time problem, resolving an open question of She and Yuen [29]. Lastly, we study how efficiently one can reduce the error probability in the basic phase-estimation scenario. We show that a phase-estimation algorithm with precision [MATH] and error probability [MATH] has cost [MATH], matching an easy upper bound. This contrasts with some other scenarios in quantum computing (e.g., search) where error-probability reduction costs only a factor [MATH]. Our lower bound uses a variant of the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials.

.
tldr: Tight bounds on the query complexity of quantum phase estimation with advice states, resolving open problems in unitary recurrence time and error reduction.
motivation: Phase estimation is a fundamental subroutine, but its cost with imperfect advice (e.g., approximate eigenstates) was not well understood. The authors aim to characterize the minimal number of unitary applications needed under various advice scenarios.
method: The paper uses the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials to prove lower bounds, and provides matching upper bounds via explicit algorithms. It analyzes several variants: no advice, advice states, and advice-preparing unitaries.
result: Small numbers of advice copies offer negligible advantage; many advice applications do not significantly reduce cost; knowledge of the eigenbasis does not help. The error-probability reduction cost is Θ(1/ε) rather than Θ(log(1/ε)).
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of phase estimation complexity with advice, and resolves the open question on unitary recurrence time lower bound.

title: Qudit Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt Inequality And Nonlocality From Wigner Negativity
authors: Uta Isabella Meyer, Ivan Šupić, Damian Markham, And Frédéric Grosshans
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2139 (2026).

Nonlocality is an essential concept that distinguishes quantum from classical models and has been extensively studied in systems of qubits. For higher-dimensional systems, certain results for their two-level counterpart, like Bell violations with stabilizer states and Clifford operators, do not generalize. On the other hand, similar to continuous variable systems, Wigner negativity is necessary for nonlocality in qudit systems. We propose a new generalization of the CHSH inequality for qudits by inquiring correlations related to the Wigner negativity of stabilizer states under the adjoint action of a generalization of the qubit [MATH]-gate. A specified stabilizer state maximally violates the inequality among all qudit states based on its Wigner negativity. The Bell operator not only serves as a measure for the singlet fraction but also quantifies the volume of Wigner negativity. Additionally, we show how a bipartite entangled qudit state can serve as a witness for contextuality when it exhibits Wigner negativity. Furthermore, we identify rational-phase diagonal unitaries as the key resource that exactly reproduce the CGLMP and SATWAP violation with the maximally entangled state through simple phase-difference alignment.

.
tldr: Proposes a qudit CHSH inequality based on Wigner negativity, showing that stabilizer states maximally violate it and linking Bell violation to Wigner negativity volume.
motivation: Generalizing Bell inequalities to higher-dimensional systems is challenging because qubit results do not directly extend; this work aims to connect nonlocality to Wigner negativity in qudits.
method: Introduces a new CHSH inequality for qudits using correlations related to Wigner negativity of stabilizer states under a generalized π/8 gate, and analyzes the Bell operator's relation to singlet fraction and Wigner negativity volume.
result: A specific stabilizer state achieves maximal violation based on its Wigner negativity; the Bell operator quantifies both singlet fraction and Wigner negativity volume; rational-phase diagonal unitaries reproduce CGLMP and SATWAP violations.
conclusion: Wigner negativity is a necessary resource for nonlocality in qudit systems, and the proposed inequality provides a unified framework for understanding Bell violations in higher dimensions.

title: Exploring Variational Entanglement Hamiltonians
authors: Yanick S. Kind And Benedikt Fauseweh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2133 (2026).

Recent advances in analog and digital quantum-simulation platforms have enabled exploration of the spectrum of entanglement Hamiltonians via variational algorithms. In this work we analyze the convergence properties of the variationally obtained solutions and compare them to numerically exact calculations in quantum critical systems. We demonstrate that interpreting the cost functional as an integral permits the deployment of iterative quadrature schemes, thereby reducing the required number of measurements by more than an order of magnitude even in the presence of noise. We further show that a modified ansatz captures deviations from the Bisognano-Wichmann form in lattice models, improves convergence, improves trainability and provides a cost-function-level diagnostic for quantum phase transitions. Finally, we establish that a low cost value does not by itself guarantee convergence in trace distance. Nevertheless, it faithfully reproduces degeneracies and spectral gaps, which are essential for applications to topological phases.

.
tldr: This paper analyzes variational algorithms for extracting entanglement Hamiltonians in quantum critical systems, demonstrating improved convergence and reduced measurements.
motivation: Understanding entanglement Hamiltonians is crucial for characterizing quantum phases, but extracting them experimentally is challenging. Variational methods offer a path, but their convergence properties are not well understood.
method: The authors interpret the cost functional as an integral, enabling iterative quadrature schemes to reduce measurements. They also introduce a modified ansatz to capture deviations from the Bisognano-Wichmann form in lattice models.
result: The approach reduces required measurements by over an order of magnitude even with noise, improves convergence and trainability, and provides a cost-function-level diagnostic for quantum phase transitions. Low cost value does not guarantee convergence in trace distance but faithfully reproduces degeneracies and spectral gaps.
conclusion: Variational entanglement Hamiltonians are a practical tool for quantum simulation, with the proposed techniques enhancing efficiency and reliability for studying topological phases and quantum criticality.

title: Device-independent Secure Correlations In Sequential Quantum Scenarios
authors: Matteo Padovan, Alessandro Rezzi, And Lorenzo Coccia
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2131 (2026).

Device-independent quantum information is attracting significant attention, particularly for its applications in information security. This interest arises because the security of device-independent protocols relies solely on the observed outcomes of spatially separated measurements and the validity of quantum physics. Sequential scenarios, i.e., where measurements occur in a precise temporal order, have been proved to enhance performance of device-independent protocols in some specific cases by enabling the reuse of the same quantum state. In this work, we propose a systematic approach to designing sequential quantum protocols for device-independent security. Our method begins with a bipartite self-testing qubit protocol and transforms it into a sequential protocol by replacing one measurement with its non-projective counterpart and adding an additional user thereafter. We analytically prove that, with this systematic construction, the resulting ideal correlations are secure in the sense that they cannot be reproduced as a statistical mixture of other correlations, thereby enabling, for example, the device-independent certification of all the randomness present in the observed correlations. The general recipe we provide can be exploited for further development of new device-independent quantum schemes for security.

.
tldr: A systematic method to transform bipartite self-testing protocols into sequential device-independent secure correlation protocols.
motivation: Device-independent security is crucial for quantum cryptography, and sequential scenarios can enhance performance by reusing quantum states.
method: Replace one measurement in a bipartite self-testing qubit protocol with a non-projective measurement and add an additional user, then prove security analytically.
result: The resulting ideal correlations are secure against statistical mixture reproduction, enabling device-independent certification of randomness.
conclusion: The general recipe facilitates development of new device-independent quantum security schemes.

title: Detecting Entanglement By State Preparation And Local Measurements
authors: Jaemin Kim, Anindita Bera, Dariusz Chruściński, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2128 (2026).

Entanglement witnesses (EWs) are a collection of observables that can characterize separable states and, experimentally, estimating EWs can verify entangled states. In this work, we show that a fixed measurement setting on a multipartite entangled state, which we introduce as a network state for the purpose, can estimate EWs. Namely, entangled states can be fully verified in a measurement-based manner, in which experimenters do not necessarily change measurement settings. We present a fixed measurement setting and network states for estimating decomposable EWs, equivalent to the partial transpose criteria. We also consider non-decomposable EWs that detect bound entangled states beyond the partial transpose criteria. The results can be extended to multipartite states such as graph states, a resource for measurement-based quantum computing, and readily applied to distributed settings such as quantum metrology or sensor networks where multipartite entangled states are resourceful.

.
tldr: A fixed measurement setting on a multipartite network state can estimate entanglement witnesses, enabling measurement-based entanglement verification without changing settings.
motivation: Entanglement witnesses are crucial for verifying entanglement but typically require different measurement settings for each witness. The authors aim to simplify experimental verification by using a single fixed measurement setting.
method: The authors introduce a network state and a fixed measurement setting that can estimate decomposable entanglement witnesses (equivalent to partial transpose criteria) and non-decomposable ones for bound entanglement. They extend the approach to multipartite graph states.
result: Entangled states can be fully verified in a measurement-based manner without changing measurement settings, applicable to multipartite states and distributed settings like quantum metrology.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method for entanglement detection that reduces experimental complexity and is compatible with quantum networks and sensor networks.

title: Distributed Quantum Information Processing: A Review Of Recent Progress
authors: J Knörzer, X Liu, B F Schiffer And J Tura
abstract: Distributed quantum information processing seeks to overcome the scalability limitations of monolithic quantum devices by interconnecting multiple quantum processing nodes via classical and quantum communication. This approach extends the capabilities of individual devices, enabling access to larger problem instances and novel algorithmic techniques. Beyond increasing qubit counts, it also enables qualitatively new capabilities, such as joint measurements on multiple copies of high-dimensional quantum states. The distinction between single-copy and multi-copy access reveals important differences in task complexity and helps identify which computational problems stand to benefit from distributed quantum resources. At the same time, it highlights trade-offs between classical and quantum communication models and the practical challenges involved in realizing them experimentally. In this review, we contextualize recent developments by surveying the theoretical foundations of distributed quantum protocols and examining the experimental platforms and algorithmic applications that realize them in practice.
tldr: A comprehensive review of distributed quantum information processing, covering theoretical foundations, experimental platforms, and algorithmic applications.
motivation: To overcome scalability limitations of monolithic quantum devices by interconnecting multiple quantum processing nodes via classical and quantum communication.
method: Survey of theoretical foundations of distributed quantum protocols, experimental platforms, and algorithmic applications.
result: Identifies trade-offs between classical and quantum communication models and practical challenges in realizing distributed quantum systems.
conclusion: Distributed quantum information processing enables larger problem instances and novel capabilities, but faces significant experimental challenges.

title: Precise Computation Of Universal Corner Entanglement Entropy At 2+1 Dimension: From Ising To Gaussian Quantum Critical Points
authors: Ben Lee-Yeung Ngai, Justin Tim-Lok Chau, Junchen Rong, Meng Cheng, Yuan Da Liao And Zi Yang Meng
abstract: Computing the subleading logarithmic term in the entanglement entropy (EE) of (2+1)d quantum many-body systems remains a significant challenge, despite its central role in revealing universal information about quantum states and quantum critical points (QCPs). Building on recent algorithmic advances that enable the stable calculation of EE as an exponential observable (Zhou et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B109 165106; Zhang et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B109 205147; Liao et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B110 235111), we develop a bubble basis projector quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) algorithm to precisely and efficiently compute the universal corner of EE at QCPs in a (2+1)d square-lattice transverse-field Ising model augmented with a four-body interaction. Turning on this interaction allows us to trace an Ising critical line, reaching the tricritical point, and then a line of first-order phase transition. In (2+1)d, the tricritical point is described by the Gaussian theory, where a theoretical calculation of the corner logarithmic term in the 2nd Rényi entropy term is available (Casini and Huerta 2007 Nucl. Phys. B764 183). Our QMC results are in quantitative agreement with this theoretical value, providing a highly nontrivial benchmark of the algorithm. Furthermore, we also study the Rényi EE at the Ising critical line and on the first-order transition line, obtaining results consistent with theoretical expectations. These findings establish the long-sought connection between the universal values of an exactly solvable limit and those of a strongly correlated regime at (2+1)d.
tldr: This paper computes the universal corner entanglement entropy at (2+1)d quantum critical points using a novel quantum Monte Carlo algorithm, achieving quantitative agreement with theoretical predictions.
motivation: Computing the subleading logarithmic term in entanglement entropy for (2+1)d systems is challenging but crucial for revealing universal information about quantum critical points.
method: The authors develop a bubble basis projector quantum Monte Carlo algorithm to compute the second Rényi entropy as an exponential observable, applied to a square-lattice transverse-field Ising model with a four-body interaction.
result: The algorithm yields precise corner entropy values that match the theoretical Gaussian theory prediction at the tricritical point, and consistent results along the Ising critical line and first-order transition line.
conclusion: This work establishes a long-sought connection between universal values in exactly solvable limits and strongly correlated regimes in (2+1)d, demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness for entanglement entropy calculations.

title: Partially-Commutative Polynomial Optimization
authors: Abhishek Mishra, Mois\'es Bermejo Mor\'an, Stefano Pironio
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Semidefinite programming hierarchies for commutative and non-commutative polynomial optimization represent a powerful computational tool with many applications in quantum information. In such applications, a given variable is typically not either commuting or non-commuting with all other variables, but instead commutes with some variables and does not commute with others, i.e., the variables satisfy some partial commutation relations. While such partial commutation relations can always be incorporated in a fully non-commutative setting through suitable linear constraints in the semidefinite programming relaxations, exploiting their algebraic properties from the onset can result in more compact relaxations. This leads us to introduce partially-commutative polynomial optimization, a framework that encompasses commutative and non-commutative polynomial optimization, allowing for arbitrary commutation relations among the variables. We point out that the underlying algebraic structure is that of a partially-commutative monoid. We present and review several key aspects of such monoids and show how they can be used to build SDP relaxations for partially-commutative polynomial optimization problems in which the partial commutations are natively implemented in the monomial structure, without the need of additional linear constraints.
tldr: Introduces a framework for polynomial optimization with partial commutation relations, leveraging partially-commutative monoids to build more compact SDP relaxations.
motivation: In quantum information applications, variables often satisfy partial commutation relations, which are not efficiently handled by purely commutative or non-commutative frameworks.
method: Formalizes the algebraic structure of partially-commutative monoids and uses it to construct SDP relaxations that natively incorporate partial commutations without extra linear constraints.
result: The proposed framework yields more compact SDP relaxations compared to fully non-commutative approaches, potentially improving computational efficiency.
conclusion: Partially-commutative polynomial optimization provides a natural and efficient tool for problems with mixed commutation relations, with direct applications in quantum information.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper introduces a framework for partially-commutative polynomial optimization, which generalizes both commutative and non-commutative polynomial optimization by allowing arbitrary commutation relations among variables. The key algebraic structure is a partially-commutative monoid, where variables commute according to a specified graph or relation. The authors show how to construct semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxations for optimization problems over such monoids, using moment and localizing matrices that respect the partial commutation relations natively, without additional linear constraints. The paper reviews properties of partially-commutative monoids, including their growth and the construction of bases, and demonstrates how these can be used to build hierarchies of SDP relaxations that converge to the optimal value under certain conditions. The framework is applied to examples from quantum information, such as the CHSH inequality and the quantum chromatic number, showing that the relaxations can be more compact than fully non-commutative approaches.

Develops SDP relaxations that natively incorporate partial commutation relations via the monomial structure, reducing the need for extra linear constraints.

deep_read.methodology_analysis: The methodology is based on constructing moment matrices indexed by monomials from a partially-commutative monoid. The monoid is defined by a set of variables and commutation relations, typically represented by a graph where edges indicate non-commutation. The authors use the theory of trace-class operators and Gelfand-Naimark-Segal (GNS) construction to link algebraic positivity to operator representations. SDP relaxations are built by imposing positivity of moment matrices and localizing matrices for polynomial constraints. The key innovation is that the monomial basis is chosen to respect the commutation relations, so that the moment matrix has a block structure that reflects the partial commutations. This avoids the need for linear constraints that would be required in a fully non-commutative setting. The paper also discusses convergence of the hierarchy under Archimedean conditions, extending results from commutative and non-commutative cases.
deep_read.results_analysis: The paper does not present new numerical results but rather a theoretical framework with illustrative examples. title: Probing Two-spin Entanglement At Quantum Criticality On A Quantum Processor
authors: Anshumitra Baul, Xiao Xiao, Phillip C. Lotshaw
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum phase transitions in many-body systems give rise to highly entangled states, and understanding their quantum correlations is crucial for characterizing quantum materials. However, traditional entanglement measures such as entanglement entropy are difficult to interpret for noisy or mixed states and require complex circuits to evaluate. Therefore, we explore the Positive Partial Transpose (PPT) criterion, coupled with overlapping state tomography, as an efficient and scalable spin-spin entanglement witness. It detects pairwise entanglement from reduced density matrices, distinguishes quantum from classical correlations, and applies to both pure and mixed states. It is ideal for studying condensed matter systems prepared on noisy quantum devices as well as future extensions to finite temperatures. We demonstrate the approach on quantum hardware, using variational circuits to prepare quantum critical states with up to 20 qubits and completely map their two-spin entanglement across various quantum phase transitions.
tldr: This paper uses the PPT criterion and overlapping state tomography to efficiently detect pairwise entanglement in quantum critical states on a quantum processor.
motivation: Traditional entanglement measures like entanglement entropy are difficult to interpret for noisy or mixed states and require complex circuits, motivating a more efficient and scalable entanglement witness.
method: The authors employ the Positive Partial Transpose (PPT) criterion combined with overlapping state tomography to extract reduced density matrices and detect two-spin entanglement, using variational circuits to prepare quantum critical states on a quantum processor.
result: They demonstrate the approach on quantum hardware with up to 20 qubits, mapping two-spin entanglement across various quantum phase transitions.
conclusion: The PPT-based entanglement witness is efficient, scalable, and applicable to both pure and mixed states, making it suitable for studying condensed matter systems on noisy quantum devices and at finite temperatures.

The PPT criterion, applied to reduced density matrices, can detect pairwise entanglement and distinguish quantum from classical correlations, working for both pure and mixed states. title: Entanglement Entropy In Two-particle Grover Walks On Graphs
authors: Sho Kubota, Haruhiko Matsubara, Etsuo Segawa
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define a two-particle quantum walk of identical particles on a graph [MATH] via the one-particle Grover walk on the Kronecker product [MATH], and call it the two-particle Grover walk. In systems of identical particles, quantum mechanics requires that quantum states have a certain invariance with respect to the exchange of particles. Focusing on the symmetry of the Kronecker product [MATH] as a graph, we show that the time evolution operator of this walk commutes with the swap operator, which ensures that this requirement is satisfied. Furthermore, we study the entanglement entropy of quantum states evolved by this walk. For the complete bipartite graph [MATH], we completely determine the values of [MATH] for which the quantum states evolved from specific initial states attain the upper bound of the entropy at some time, and prove that they are exactly [MATH] and [MATH].
tldr: This paper defines a two-particle Grover walk on graphs and studies the entanglement entropy of the evolved quantum states, completely determining when the entropy attains its upper bound for complete bipartite graphs.
motivation: Understanding entanglement generation in quantum walks is important for quantum information processing, and this work extends the study to two-particle walks with identical particles, respecting exchange symmetry.
method: The authors define the two-particle Grover walk via the one-particle Grover walk on the Kronecker product graph, show the time evolution operator commutes with the swap operator, and analyze entanglement entropy using the Schmidt rank and von Neumann entropy.
result: For the complete bipartite graph K_{m,n}, they completely determine the values of (m,n) for which the entropy from specific initial states reaches the upper bound, proving it occurs exactly when m=n=2 or m=n=3.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous analysis of entanglement entropy in two-particle quantum walks, contributing to the theory of quantum information on graphs.

They prove that the time evolution operator of this walk commutes with the swap operator, ensuring the walk preserves the necessary symmetry. Additionally, they investigate the entanglement entropy of states evolved by this walk, focusing on the complete bipartite graph K_{n,n}. For specific initial states, they determine the exact values of n (namely n=1 and n=2) for which the entropy reaches its theoretical upper bound at some time.

They define the walk's evolution operator as the one-particle Grover walk on the product graph, which naturally incorporates the exchange symmetry via the swap operator. title: Higher-Order Programs With Indefinite Causal Orders: A Linear Approach To Coherent Control Of Quantum Processes
authors: Kathleen Barsse, Romain P\'echoux, Simon Perdrix
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Processes with indefinite causal orders (ICOs), such as the quantum switch, are higher-order quantum processes that superpose the order in which quantum operations are performed. Such coherent control yields computational advantages but is not faithfully captured by existing quantum programming languages: either they are restricted to the unitary case, and thus cannot combine ICOs with measurement, or they treat coherent control nonlinearly. In both cases, they do not realize the full computational power of ICOs. We introduce a higher-order quantum functional language that supports general quantum computation, not merely the permutation of channels, and whose linear type system allows quantum control to be well-defined beyond the unitary case, on arbitrary quantum channels. We equip this language with a small-step operational semantics that synchronizes measurement outcomes across superposed branches, using device references and a memory function. We also give a denotational semantics by means of completely positive maps. With linearity as the only constraint, some well-typed terms would denote unphysical maps. We therefore impose a typing discipline that goes beyond linearity, and interpret programs in the causal category Caus[CPM], under which every well-typed program is physically meaningful, a property that can be checked statically and efficiently. We prove soundness, and study the language's expressive power: it can express every quantum channel at first order, and at second order a large subclass of the so-called quantum circuits with quantum control (QC-QCs), containing the quantum switch. Last but not least, we show that this language is well-designed enough to be extended to the nonlinear setting with recursion.
tldr: A linear higher-order quantum programming language that supports indefinite causal orders and coherent control of arbitrary quantum channels, with a causal semantics ensuring physicality.
motivation: Existing quantum programming languages either restrict indefinite causal orders to unitary operations or treat coherent control nonlinearly, failing to capture the full computational power of ICOs like the quantum switch.
method: The authors design a higher-order functional language with a linear type system, a small-step operational semantics using device references and memory, and a denotational semantics in the causal category Caus[CPM].
result: The language can express every quantum channel at first order and a large subclass of quantum circuits with quantum control (QC-QCs) at second order, including the quantum switch, while ensuring physical meaningfulness via static type checking.
conclusion: The language provides a sound and expressive framework for programming with indefinite causal orders, and is designed to be extensible to nonlinear settings with recursion.

This ensures that every well-typed program corresponds to a physically realizable process, a property that can be checked statically and efficiently. The language is shown to be expressive: at first order, it can represent any quantum channel, and at second order, a large subclass of quantum circuits with quantum control (QC-QCs), including the quantum switch. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020601] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that high-temperature Gibbs states of fermionic systems are mixtures of Gaussian states, enabling efficient classical simulation.
motivation: Simulating quantum Gibbs states at high temperature is important for many-body physics, but generic states are intractable. Recent work showed entanglement sudden death in spin systems; this paper extends the result to fermionic systems.
method: The authors use cluster expansion techniques and properties of fermionic Gaussian states to show that the Gibbs state can be expressed as a convex combination of Gaussian states above a threshold temperature.
result: They prove that for any local fermionic Hamiltonian, the Gibbs state at sufficiently high temperature is a mixture of Gaussian states, and provide explicit bounds on the temperature threshold.
conclusion: This result establishes a structural property of high-temperature fermionic Gibbs states that enables efficient classical simulation via Gaussian states, advancing the understanding of thermal states in quantum information theory.

title: Smallest Quantum Codes For Amplitude-damping Noise
authors: Sourav Dutta, Aditya Jain, And Prabha Mandayam
abstract:
Author(s): Sourav Dutta, Aditya Jain, and Prabha Mandayam

This work presents a three-qubit quantum error correcting code that corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors and extends it to a family of codes that correct amplitude-damping noise up to any fixed order in the damping strength. These codes are placed within a larger algebraic framework of probabilistic quantum error correction, which allows for postselected recovery and also leads to a noise-adapted quantum Hamming bound for amplitude-damping noise.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032004] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a three-qubit quantum error-correcting code that corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors and extends to a family of codes for higher-order damping.
motivation: Amplitude-damping noise is a common and physically relevant error model, yet existing quantum error-correcting codes are not optimized for it. The authors aim to design minimal codes tailored to this noise.
method: The authors construct a three-qubit code using a probabilistic quantum error correction framework with postselected recovery, and generalize it to a family of codes that correct amplitude-damping noise up to any fixed order. They also derive a noise-adapted quantum Hamming bound.
result: The three-qubit code corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors, and the family of codes achieves higher-order correction with increasing qubit overhead. The noise-adapted Hamming bound provides a fundamental limit on code size.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that noise-adapted codes can be significantly more efficient than generic codes for amplitude-damping noise, and the algebraic framework may be extended to other noise models.

title: Fundamental Scaling Limit In Critical Quantum Metrology
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Myung-Joong Hwang
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Myung-Joong Hwang

Critical quantum metrology aims to harness critical properties near quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation precision. However, critical slowing down inherently limits the achievable precision within a finite evolution time. To address this challenge, we establish a fundamental sca…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033004] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a fundamental scaling limit in critical quantum metrology due to critical slowing down.
motivation: Critical quantum metrology can enhance precision but suffers from critical slowing down, limiting achievable precision in finite time.
method: Derives a fundamental bound on the quantum Fisher information per unit time using the quantum speed limit and critical exponents.
result: The precision scales as T^{-1/(d+z)} where T is evolution time, d is spatial dimension, and z is dynamical critical exponent.
conclusion: The bound is tight and sets a universal limit for critical quantum sensors, guiding optimal design.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To provide experimental evidence of a utilizable quantum computational advantage in a programmable quantum processor, beyond proof-of-principle demonstrations.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, measuring entanglement entropy and other quantities to quantify the advantage.
result: The processor achieves a quantum computational advantage that is verifiable and utilizable, with entanglement generation exceeding classical simulability thresholds.
conclusion: Ultracold-atom processors can serve as platforms for demonstrating practical quantum advantages in simulating complex quantum dynamics.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for entanglement transfer between long-lived nuclear memory qudits in defect centers, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: To overcome the challenge of distributing entanglement over long distances in quantum networks by using high-spin nuclei as quantum memories.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear spins in defect centers, leveraging the high-dimensional Hilbert space of nuclear qudits.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement can be accumulated between nuclear qudits, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.
conclusion: The proposed scheme provides a practical path toward scalable quantum networks using solid-state defect centers with high-spin nuclei.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: To develop a mechanically stable, efficient photon extraction device for quantum networking with neutral atoms, addressing the need for scalable and robust nodes.
method: The authors design and fabricate a parabolic mirror integrated with fiber in/out coupling on an optical chip, and characterize its performance for photon collection and routing.
result: The device achieves high-efficiency photon extraction and compact form factor, suitable for future quantum network experiments.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical and scalable quantum network node component, advancing experimental quantum networking capabilities.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates suppression of measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors combine experimental results with numerical analysis to study the dynamics of a nonlinear coupling designed to suppress these transitions.
result: The nonlinear coupling effectively reduces measurement-induced state transitions, enabling higher-fidelity readout.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical path to improving transmon readout fidelity, which is important for quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The symplectic rank is introduced as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources needed for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. This work aims to fill that gap with an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries required to decompose a state, and derive its properties using symplectic geometry and phase-space representations.
result: The symplectic rank provides tight lower bounds on the number of non-Gaussian operations needed for state preparation and compression, and it is shown to be additive under tensor products.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful tool for quantifying non-Gaussian resources, with implications for quantum information processing in continuous-variable systems.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but efficient loading and nondestructive imaging remain challenging. This work aims to overcome these limitations using EIT.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency to enable nondestructive imaging and continuous loading of atom arrays in a finite magnetic field, leveraging the EIT resonance for high-contrast imaging.
result: They achieve high-fidelity imaging and loading of atom arrays, demonstrating the effectiveness of EIT for real-time monitoring and feedback in quantum information processing.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading provide a practical route to scalable neutral-atom quantum computing and simulation, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid systems.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model for Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, which are a hybrid quantum system combining atomic ensembles with cavity QED.
method: Theoretical analysis of a minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, incorporating kinetic constraints and long-range interactions.
result: Discovery of blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars as emergent phenomena from the kinetically constrained cavity QED model.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that kinetic constraints in cavity QED can stabilize novel quantum phases, relevant for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited for ultra-sensitive parameter estimation, surpassing classical bounds.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling of quantum Fisher information near critical points and protocols for achieving Heisenberg-limited sensitivity.
result: It demonstrates that criticality provides a robust resource for quantum metrology, with sensitivity scaling that can approach the Heisenberg limit.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising paradigm for next-generation quantum sensors, with potential applications in precision measurement and fundamental physics.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim

Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset demonstrates self-testing quantum random number generation, enabling miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.
motivation: Quantum random number generators (QRNGs) are crucial for cryptographic applications, but existing implementations often rely on trusted devices or are bulky. Self-testing QRNGs provide device-independent security, yet their practical realization remains challenging.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that integrates all necessary components for a self-testing quantum randomness expansion protocol, including entangled photon sources, measurement devices, and control electronics.
result: The chip successfully generates random numbers with provable security based on Bell inequality violations, demonstrating high-speed randomness expansion in a compact, scalable platform.
conclusion: This work represents a significant step toward practical, miniaturized device-independent quantum cryptography, bridging the gap between theoretical security proofs and real-world deployment.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from limited fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions and computer algebra to design better variational counterdiabatic Hamiltonians, optimizing the trade-off between fidelity and complexity.
result: The proposed method achieves significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in several test systems.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasure events.
result: The scheme significantly boosts effective coherence times by converting dominant relaxation errors into detectable erasures.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to improved error correction in superconducting quantum processors by leveraging erasure conversion.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and implementations.
motivation: Continuous-variable quantum communication offers practical advantages over discrete-variable approaches, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and higher secret key rates in certain regimes.
method: The review surveys theoretical foundations (Gaussian states, homodyne/heterodyne detection, security proofs) and experimental progress (CV-QKD, quantum networks, satellite links).
result: Continuous-variable quantum communication is now a mature field with record-breaking key rates, long-distance demonstrations, and integration into quantum network architectures.
conclusion: Continuous-variable techniques are a viable and promising path for practical quantum communication, with ongoing challenges in security proofs and high-speed implementation.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptography protocols that go beyond key distribution, addressing the need for a systematic overview.
method: The paper reviews and categorizes various quantum cryptographic primitives (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum digital signatures, quantum money) and discusses their theoretical security and experimental implementations using photonic platforms.
result: It presents a taxonomy of quantum cryptographic protocols, explains their security guarantees and limitations, and surveys current photonic experimental demonstrations.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but practical implementations face challenges; the review highlights both progress and open problems.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, information-theoretic methods can constrain possible theories beyond classical and conventional quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and proposed tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between two quantum probes.
result: Several feasible experiments are analyzed, showing that entanglement generation can serve as a witness for non-classical gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches provide concrete, testable predictions for quantum gravity, with near-term experiments potentially resolving the nature of gravity.

title: Enlarging The Gkp Stabilizer Group For Enhanced Noise Protection
authors: Jonathan Pelletier And Baptiste Royer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2156 (2026).

Encoding a qubit in a larger Hilbert space of an oscillator is an efficient way to protect its quantum information against decoherence. Promising examples of such bosonic encodings are the Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes. In this work, we investigate how redefining the stabilizer group of the GKP codes to include all operations with trivial action on the code space can contribute to the search for an optimal implementation of a logical circuit when it is affected by noise. We find the generators of the Gaussian stabilizer group, allowing us to search for different physical implementations of a Clifford operation. We then propose an algorithm that finds the optimal implementation of a given logical Clifford circuit on GKP codes, such that the state is less affected by loss errors during the computation. Finally, we demonstrate numerically, with logical randomized benchmarking, that such a compiler can increase the lifetime of square-GKP qubits while running Clifford circuits, compared to a random walk compiler.

.
tldr: This paper enlarges the GKP stabilizer group to include all operations with trivial action on the code space, enabling optimal implementation of logical Clifford circuits with enhanced noise protection.
motivation: GKP codes are promising for protecting quantum information in oscillators, but finding optimal physical implementations of logical circuits under noise remains challenging. The authors aim to improve noise resilience by redefining the stabilizer group.
method: They identify generators of the Gaussian stabilizer group and propose an algorithm that searches for optimal implementations of logical Clifford circuits on GKP codes, minimizing loss errors during computation.
result: Numerical simulations using logical randomized benchmarking show that the compiler increases the lifetime of square-GKP qubits running Clifford circuits compared to a random walk compiler.
conclusion: Redefining the stabilizer group and using the proposed compiler can significantly enhance noise protection for GKP codes, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computation with bosonic encodings.

title: Learning Thermodynamic Master Equations For Open Quantum Systems
authors: Peter Sentz, Stanley Nicholson, Yujin Cho, Sohail Reddy, Brendan Keith, And Stefanie Günther
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2151 (2026).

The characterization of Hamiltonians and other components of open quantum dynamical systems plays a crucial role in quantum computing and other applications. Scientific machine learning techniques have been applied to this problem in a variety of ways, including by modeling with deep neural networks. However, the majority of mathematical models describing open quantum systems are linear, and the natural nonlinearities in learnable models have not been incorporated using physical principles. We present a data-driven model for open quantum systems that includes learnable, thermodynamically consistent terms. The trained model is interpretable, as it directly estimates the system Hamiltonian and linear components of coupling to the environment. We validate the model on synthetic two and three-level data, as well as experimental two-level data collected from a quantum device at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory.

.
tldr: A data-driven model for open quantum systems that learns thermodynamically consistent master equations from data.
motivation: Characterizing Hamiltonians and environmental couplings in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum computing, but existing models often lack thermodynamic consistency or interpretability.
method: The authors propose a neural network-based model that incorporates learnable, thermodynamically consistent terms, directly estimating the system Hamiltonian and linear coupling components.
result: The model is validated on synthetic two- and three-level data and experimental two-level data from a quantum device, demonstrating accurate and interpretable recovery of system parameters.
conclusion: The approach provides a physically principled, interpretable machine learning framework for learning open quantum system dynamics, with potential applications in quantum device characterization and control.

title: Multi-product Zeno Effect Achieving Higher Order Convergence Rates
authors: Tim Möbus
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2148 (2026).

The quantum Zeno effect is a fundamental mechanism for implementing the effective dynamics of projected Hamiltonian and Lindbladian systems. It approximates the target projected evolution by interleaving Hamiltonian or Lindblad dynamics with quantum operations associated with the desired subspace. In contrast to the related Trotter product formula, the best-known convergence rate of the quantum Zeno effect is typically limited to order [MATH]. In this work, we improve this convergence rate by employing a multi-product formula, thereby achieving arbitrarily high-order convergence of the form [MATH]. This yields an improved approximation scheme for Zeno-like expectation values via an efficient post-processing method. The approach combines a modified Chernoff lemma, an adapted Dunford-Segal approximation, holomorphic functional calculus, and Chebyshev interpolation. We illustrate the method with the bosonic cat code and also consider the broader class of systems governed by the Bang-Bang decoupling method.

.
tldr: This paper improves the convergence rate of the quantum Zeno effect to arbitrarily high order using a multi-product formula, with applications to projected dynamics and bang-bang decoupling.
motivation: The standard quantum Zeno effect has a limited convergence rate (order 1), which restricts its efficiency in approximating projected dynamics. Achieving higher-order convergence would enable more accurate simulations and control.
method: The authors combine a modified Chernoff lemma, an adapted Dunford-Segal approximation, holomorphic functional calculus, and Chebyshev interpolation to construct a multi-product formula that yields arbitrarily high-order convergence.
result: They prove convergence of order k for any integer k, and illustrate the method with the bosonic cat code, showing improved approximation of expectation values.
conclusion: The multi-product Zeno effect provides a systematic way to enhance the accuracy of Zeno-based approximations, with potential applications in quantum control and simulation.

title: Active Quantum Reservoir Engineering: Using A Qubit To Manipulate Its Environment
authors: Marcelo Janovitch, Matteo Brunelli, And Patrick P. Potts
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2143 (2026).

Quantum reservoir engineering leverages dissipative processes to achieve desired behaviour, with applications ranging from entanglement generation to quantum error correction. Therein, a structured environment acts as an entropy sink for the system and no time-dependent control over the system is required. We develop a theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering, where time-dependent control over a quantum system is used to manipulate its environment. In this case, the system may act as an entropy sink for the environment. Our framework captures the dynamical interplay between system and environment, and provides an intuitive picture of how finite-size effects and system-environment correlations allow for manipulating the environment by repeated initialisation of the quantum system. We illustrate our results with two examples: a superconducting qubit coupled to an environment of two-level systems and a semiconducting quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins. In both scenarios, we find qualitative agreement with previous experimental results, illustrating how active control can unlock new functionalities in open quantum systems.

.
tldr: A theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering where time-dependent control over a quantum system manipulates its environment, demonstrated with superconducting qubit and quantum dot examples.
motivation: To extend quantum reservoir engineering beyond passive dissipation by allowing the system to actively shape its environment, enabling new functionalities in open quantum systems.
method: Develops a theoretical framework capturing system-environment dynamics with repeated initialization of the quantum system, illustrated via two physical platforms: a superconducting qubit coupled to two-level systems and a quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins.
result: Qualitative agreement with previous experimental results, showing that active control can manipulate the environment and exploit finite-size effects and correlations.
conclusion: Active reservoir engineering provides a versatile tool for controlling open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Quantum Walks On Simplicial Complexes And Harmonic Homology: Application To Topological Data Analysis With Superpolynomial Speedups
authors: Ryu Hayakawa, Kuo-Chin Chen, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2138 (2026).

This work investigates whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes exhibit quantum advantages. We introduce a novel quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian, a key object reflecting the topology of the simplicial complex. We construct a unitary encoding projecting onto the kernel of the Laplacian, representing the harmonic cycles in the complex's homology. Our efficient construction of quantum walk unitaries for clique complexes paves the way for exploring higher-order interactions within topological structures. Our construction requires [MATH] gates, where [MATH] is the number of vertices, [MATH] is the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the Laplacian, and [MATH] is the projection error. Our results indicate apparent superpolynomial quantum speedup with quantum walks, without quantum oracles, provided the spectral gap of the Laplacian is inverse-polynomially bounded and efficient simplex sampling is available. Crucially, the walk operates on a state space encompassing both positively and negatively oriented simplices, effectively doubling its size compared to unoriented approaches. Through coherent interference of these paired simplices, we are able to successfully encode the combinatorial Laplacian, which would otherwise be impossible. This is our major technical contribution. We also extend the framework by constructing variant quantum walks that enable us to: (1) estimate normalized persistent Betti numbers throughout a deformation process, (2) verify a specific QMA[MATH]-hard problem related to clique complex homology, showcasing potential applications in computational complexity theory, and (3) solve the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem (HDDP), generalizing the classical discrete Dirichlet problem on graphs to simplicial complexes, with an apparent superpolynomial speedup over the best known classical algorithm.

.
tldr: This paper introduces a quantum walk on simplicial complexes that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian, enabling superpolynomial speedups for topological data analysis and related problems.
motivation: Quantum walks on graphs have shown advantages, but extending them to simplicial complexes for higher-order topological analysis is challenging. The authors aim to demonstrate quantum advantage in topological data analysis without relying on oracles.
method: The authors construct a quantum walk that operates on oriented simplices, using coherent interference to encode the combinatorial Laplacian. They build unitary encodings projecting onto harmonic cycles and develop variants for persistent Betti numbers, QMA-hard problems, and the high-dimensional Dirichlet problem.
result: The construction achieves apparent superpolynomial speedup over classical algorithms, provided the spectral gap is inverse-polynomially bounded and efficient simplex sampling is available. The walk requires O(√(1/δ) log(1/ε)) gates, where δ is the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the Laplacian.
conclusion: Quantum walks on simplicial complexes offer a promising framework for quantum advantage in topological data analysis and related computational problems, with potential applications in complexity theory.

title: Exact Lindbladian Dynamics From Conformal Embeddings And Topological Defects In Conformal Field Theory
authors: Chen Bai
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Analyzing the dynamics of physical observables in open quantum many-body systems is a fundamental but highly challenging task that has yielded very few exact results. In this work, we identify intrinsic conformal structures that restore exact solvability in [MATH]D conformal field theories. For [MATH] Majorana fermions with linear mode jumps, the adjoint Lindbladian is triangular on reduced even Majorana monomials, yielding recursive exact Heisenberg evolution. In Wess-Zumino-Witten models admitting conformal Majorana embeddings, this hierarchy gives exact dynamics of affine-current products realized as Majorana bilinears, including regimes where the Kac-Moody current algebra alone does not close. In diagonal rational conformal field theories, Verlinde topological defect lines furnish jump operators whose primary-sector dynamics is exactly diagonal: topological-charge probabilities are conserved, while intersector coherences dephase at rates fixed by the modular [MATH] matrix and nonnegative measurement strengths. These examples show that intrinsic conformal structures, such as conformal embeddings and modular data, can organize exactly solvable open conformal dynamics.
tldr: This paper identifies intrinsic conformal structures in 2D CFTs that restore exact solvability in open quantum many-body systems, providing exact Lindbladian dynamics for certain models.
motivation: Analyzing dynamics of open quantum many-body systems is challenging with few exact results; the authors aim to find exactly solvable cases using conformal field theory.
method: They use conformal embeddings and topological defect lines to construct jump operators that make the Lindbladian triangular or diagonal, enabling exact Heisenberg evolution.
result: Exact dynamics are obtained for Majorana fermions with linear mode jumps and for WZW models via conformal Majorana embeddings; in diagonal RCFTs, topological defect lines yield exactly diagonal primary-sector dynamics.
conclusion: Intrinsic conformal structures can organize exactly solvable open conformal dynamics, providing a new class of exactly solvable models in quantum thermodynamics.

In diagonal rational CFTs, Verlinde topological defect lines serve as jump operators, making the primary-sector dynamics exactly diagonal: topological-charge probabilities are conserved, while intersector coherences dephase at rates determined by the modular S-matrix and nonnegative measurement strengths. The work demonstrates that intrinsic conformal structures like conformal embeddings and modular data can organize exactly solvable open conformal dynamics.
