title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and their multimessenger implications.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, with connections to electromagnetic astronomy and nuclear astrophysics.
method: The paper surveys detection prospects for future gravitational-wave detectors and discusses simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It highlights the potential for multimessenger observations to improve our understanding of neutron star interiors and dense matter.
conclusion: Multimessenger astronomy with continuous gravitational waves will be an important area for future detectors.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental constraints and discovery potential.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for physics beyond the Standard Model, and the HL-LHC offers a new opportunity to search for it.
method: The authors survey current experimental constraints and theoretical developments, and project discovery potential across multiple search channels and scenarios.
result: Stringent bounds have narrowed the viable parameter space, but the HL-LHC can still probe well-motivated models.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains viable and the HL-LHC will provide crucial tests.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion and neutrino production.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The review synthesizes theoretical and experimental work from the last decade on nuclear reactions, plasma physics, and atomic physics in the solar interior.
result: It provides an updated understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning and its diagnostic probes.
conclusion: The paper advances solar model predictions but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes the state of the art in low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling, resonances, and interference effects.
motivation: Nuclear reactions at stellar energies are difficult to measure directly due to very small rates, and theoretical understanding is needed to model stellar burning and nucleosynthesis.
method: The paper reviews theoretical approaches including quantum-mechanical tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses experimental techniques for studying these reactions.
result: The review provides a comprehensive overview of current theoretical and experimental methods for low-energy nuclear astrophysics.
conclusion: Advances in theory and experiment are needed to better understand stellar nuclear reactions and element formation.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: This review paper discusses self-alignment in polar active matter, a topic in soft condensed matter physics and active matter, with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Active matter systems with self-alignment exhibit novel collective behaviors, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The paper provides a unified mathematical and conceptual framework for self-alignment in active systems, reviewing existing models and experimental observations.
result: It identifies that self-alignment can lead to synchronized motion and other emergent phenomena in active matter.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a key property in active matter with potential applications in biology and robotics, but it is outside the scope of the user's research interests.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique that uses laser pulses to generate ultrasound waves for deep tissue imaging.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers high-resolution, deep-tissue optical contrast noninvasively.
method: The review covers the basic physics of optoacoustic signal generation, detection, and multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: Optoacoustic microscopy enables imaging millimeters to centimeters deep with high resolution, impacting biological and clinical research.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biomedical imaging, with ongoing developments in multimodal approaches.

title: Uniaxial-stress-induced Magnetic Transitions In The Triangular-lattice Antiferromagnet PdCrO2
authors: Nina Stilkerich, Tobias Ritschel, Hilary M L Noad, Richard Waite, Dmitry Khalyavin, Kousuke Ishida, Pascal Manuel, Fabio Orlandi, Seunghyun Khim, Elena Gati, Andrew P Mackenzie, Jochen Geck And Clifford W Hicks
abstract: Uniaxial stress is a promising method to tune magnetic frustration, allowing its effects to be studied in a precise way. In this work, uniaxial stress is applied to the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet PdCrO . The Cr–Cr magnetic interaction is very sensitive to interatomic separation, so laboratory-achievable stress can induce substantial changes in magnetic structure. Results from three types of measurement are presented: x-ray diffraction, the stress–strain relationship, and neutron diffraction. The combined data show that the elastic moduli of PdCrO are strongly affected by stress-induced changes in magnetic structure. A new, first-order stress-induced magnetic transition is observed, at which the lattice constant shrinks by 0.21%. The lattice stiffens dramatically across this transition: the Young’s modulus increases by GPa, and the Poisson ratio falls from to . This stiffening indicates that the magnetic order ‘locks,’ that is, becomes insensitive to lattice strain. This locking might occur because the new stress-induced magnetic order nests the Fermi surface of the Pd sheets. Other frustrated magnets, including candidate spin liquids, may show similarly strong coupling between magnetic and elastic degrees of freedom.
tldr: This paper studies uniaxial-stress-induced magnetic transitions in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet PdCrO2, focusing on the coupling between magnetic and elastic degrees of freedom.
motivation: To understand how uniaxial stress can tune magnetic frustration and induce new magnetic phases in frustrated magnets.
method: Combined x-ray diffraction, stress-strain measurements, and neutron diffraction under uniaxial stress.
result: A first-order stress-induced magnetic transition is observed, accompanied by a 0.21% lattice shrinkage and dramatic stiffening of the lattice.
conclusion: The magnetic order becomes locked under stress, possibly due to Fermi surface nesting, suggesting strong magnetoelastic coupling in frustrated magnets.

title: Orthogonal Phase Modulation And Lissajous Mode Decoupling In Light-induced Thermoelastic Spectroscopy For Real-time Multi-component Gas Sensing
authors: Hanxu Ma, Shunda Qiao, Ying He, Haiyue Sun And Yufei Ma
abstract: This paper proposed an optical detection mechanism that utilized orthogonal phase modulation (OPM) and Lissajous mode decoupling within a light-induced thermoelastic spectroscopy (LITES) sensor for the first time, enabling real-time multi-component gas sensing. By establishing a two-dimensional forced vibration model of a quartz tuning fork (QTF) under dual-path OPM, it revealed the vibration mode coupling mechanism induced by non-ideal phase and amplitude conditions, thereby providing a theoretical basis and optimization pathway for suppressing channel crosstalk. In the OPM-LITES sensor, two continuous-wave distributed feedback lasers were modulated by sinusoidal waves with the same frequency (f0/2, where f0 is the resonant frequency of the QTF) but a phase difference of 45°. The combined beam, after wavelength division multiplexing, co-excited the self-designed low-frequency QTF. The piezoelectric signal generated by the QTF underwent orthogonal demodulation via a lock-in amplifier (LIA). The concentration information for the two gases was independently retrieved from the decoupled X-component and Y-component of the LIA. Experimental results demonstrated that the OPM-LITES sensor exhibited excellent linear responses to both methane (CH4) and acetylene (C2H2), with average relative systematic errors of 0.54% and 0.79%, and maximum relative errors of 1.72% and 1.38%, respectively. Allan deviation analysis indicated that the minimum detection limits (MDLs) for CH4 and C2H2 reached 0.32 ppm and 0.29 ppm, with normalized noise-equivalent absorption coefficients of 5.09 × 10−9 cm−1·W·Hz−1/2 and 6.18 × 10−9 cm−1·W·Hz−1/2, respectively. This study not only provided a simple and efficient solution for real-time multi-component gas detection but also established a novel theoretical framework for mode decoupling and signal processing in spectroscopic sensing.
tldr: This paper presents a novel optical gas sensing technique using orthogonal phase modulation and Lissajous mode decoupling in light-induced thermoelastic spectroscopy for real-time multi-component gas detection.
motivation: Real-time multi-component gas sensing is important for environmental monitoring and industrial safety, but existing methods suffer from channel crosstalk and complexity.
method: The authors use two continuous-wave lasers modulated at the same frequency with a 45° phase difference to excite a quartz tuning fork, then apply orthogonal demodulation via a lock-in amplifier to decouple the signals from two gases.
result: The sensor achieves linear responses for methane and acetylene with low systematic errors (0.54% and 0.79%) and detection limits of 0.32 ppm and 0.29 ppm, respectively.
conclusion: The proposed OPM-LITES sensor provides a simple and efficient solution for real-time multi-component gas sensing with a novel theoretical framework for mode decoupling.

title: Self-similarity Of Mobility Networks
authors: Ying-Yue Lyu, Xiao-Yong Yan, Bin Jia, Jobst Heitzig, Ziyou Gao, J\"urgen Kurths
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mobility systems of people and goods are inherently multi-scale, spanning levels of organization from individual cities to regions and nations. Understanding whether mobility networks exhibit similar patterns across these scales is important. Such similarity would point to common organizing principles, enabling insights gained at one scale to inform planning and management at others. Despite growing efforts to analyze mobility at multiple scales, such cross-scale similarity remains poorly understood, and renormalization provides a natural framework for addressing this question. Here, we propose a Neighbor-Limited Box Covering method to renormalize undirected weighted mobility networks. This method iteratively selects box centers in descending order of node strength, merges each center with a fixed number of its highest-weight neighbors to form a renormalized node, and aggregates edge weights between renormalized nodes to generate the network at the next scale. We apply this technique to uncover multi-scale structures of real-world inter-city human mobility and freight trip networks in China and find that the topological structures, weighted structural features, and dynamic processes all exhibit self-similarity across these multi-scale mobility networks. Moreover, we find that the constituent nodes in most renormalized nodes show a strong spatial cohesion, and the boundaries of them closely follow existing political and socio-economic borders, even though the method does not explicitly incorporate any spatial information. Our study not only reveals the consistency of multi-scale inter-city mobility patterns, but also provides important insights into their spatial organization. Furthermore, our method is applicable to mobility networks of different sizes and has potential as a powerful tool for the multi-scale analysis of various other real-world complex systems.
tldr: This paper studies self-similarity in mobility networks using a renormalization method, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding cross-scale similarity in mobility networks can inform planning and management, but the topic is unrelated to the user's research interests.
method: A Neighbor-Limited Box Covering method is proposed to renormalize undirected weighted mobility networks by iteratively merging nodes.
result: Real-world inter-city human mobility and freight networks in China exhibit self-similarity in topology, weighted features, and dynamics.
conclusion: The method reveals consistent multi-scale patterns and spatial cohesion, but has no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Seeing Inside A Plasmonic Nanogap: Few-molecule Orientation And Preferential Adsorption
authors: Francesco Ciccarello, Nobuaki Oyamada, Thwahira Shirin Alampara, Konstantin Malchow, Christophe Galland
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Molecule-surface interactions are central to many research and technological areas, spanning from heterogeneous catalysis and polymer science to electrochemistry. Of particular relevance are metallic nanogaps used in molecular electronics and near-field spectroscopy. Due to the buried nature of these double interfaces, few methods exist to monitor side-specific interactions and relative molecular orientation inside the gap. In this work, we introduce plasmon-enhanced nonlinear vibrational spectroscopy as an efficient tool to investigate surface molecular adsorption within metallic nanojunctions. By exploiting simultaneous vibrational sum- and difference-frequency generation in dual-resonant nanocavities, we resolve molecular orientation and preferential binding to one of the two gold surfaces, with few-molecule sensitivity. We also discover that the non-resonant (electronic) second-order nonlinear response is not an intrinsic property of the metal surface, but is instead governed by the molecule-surface interaction. Our findings provide a powerful analytical tool, easily implementable as an add-on to Raman spectroscopy, thanks to commercially available mid-infrared quantum cascade lasers.
tldr: This paper uses plasmon-enhanced nonlinear vibrational spectroscopy to study molecular orientation and preferential adsorption in metallic nanogaps.
motivation: Understanding molecule-surface interactions in nanogaps is important for molecular electronics and near-field spectroscopy, but few methods can probe side-specific interactions and orientation.
method: The authors employ simultaneous vibrational sum- and difference-frequency generation in dual-resonant nanocavities to resolve molecular orientation and preferential binding with few-molecule sensitivity.
result: They demonstrate that the non-resonant electronic second-order nonlinear response is governed by molecule-surface interaction, not intrinsic to the metal surface.
conclusion: This provides a powerful analytical tool for studying molecular adsorption in nanogaps, easily integrable with Raman spectroscopy using commercial mid-infrared lasers.

title: Topological Signatures Of Imperial Collapse And Fragmentation: Administrative Dissolution, Territorial Reorganization And Early-Warning Observables In The Han Dynasty Network (206~bce\,--\,220~ce)
authors: Jose de Jesus Bernal-Alvarado, David Delepine, Carlos Pinedo Guadarrama
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the persistent homology formalism done in references~ to the Han Dynasty ([MATH]--[MATH]), testing whether the collapse threshold [MATH] and the three-network decomposition methodology established for the Roman--Byzantine case generalize to a mechanistically distinct imperial system. Three complementary networks are constructed from geospatial and historical data: an administrative network ([MATH], 392~prefectures from CHGIS~v6), a geographic network ([MATH], with node end-dates extended beyond administrative dissolution), and an 81-node Silk Road trade network ([MATH]) as a structural control. Edge costs are derived via least-cost path analysis on a [MATH] digital elevation model, modulated by five historical friction channels. [MATH] collapses to zero at 220~CE (phase~G slope [MATH], [MATH]) while [MATH] simultaneously to [MATH], producing a divergence [MATH] -- the topological signature of . The cross-network Wasserstein distance [MATH] jumps from exactly zero to [MATH] at [MATH]~CE, one decade after the Yellow Turban Rebellion, and three long-lived [MATH] cycles matching the Wei, Shu, and Wu domains emerge under the post-184~CE fragmentation model -- thirty years before formal partition. Three independent early-warning indicators (Wasserstein velocity [MATH], correlation length [MATH], and the Integrated Change Tracker) signal collapse onset 45--50~years before formal dissolution.
tldr: This paper applies topological data analysis to study the collapse of the Han Dynasty, using persistent homology on historical networks.
motivation: To test whether topological signatures of collapse observed in the Roman Empire generalize to a different imperial system.
method: Constructs administrative, geographic, and trade networks from historical data and applies persistent homology to detect collapse indicators.
result: Identifies a topological signature of collapse (divergence of Betti numbers) and early-warning indicators 45-50 years before formal dissolution.
conclusion: The methodology generalizes to the Han Dynasty, suggesting universal topological patterns in imperial collapse.

title: Asymptotic Stability Of Solutions To The Good Boussinesq Equation In Dispersive Wave Region
authors: Yingmin Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work studies the asymptotic stability of solutions to the good Boussinesq equation in dispersive wave region when the reflection coefficients associated with the initial data belong to weighted Sobolev space. The Dbar-steepest descent method is applied to the Riemann-Hilbert problem and the long-time asymptotic expansion of the solution are obtained up to an optimal error of order [MATH]. Compared with previous results, we extend the initial data from the rapidly decaying Schwartz space to a weighted Sobolev space, and prove the asymptotic stability of the solution in dispersive wave region.
tldr: This paper studies asymptotic stability of solutions to the good Boussinesq equation using the Dbar-steepest descent method.
motivation: To extend previous results on the long-time asymptotic behavior of the good Boussinesq equation from rapidly decaying Schwartz space to weighted Sobolev space.
method: Applies the Dbar-steepest descent method to the Riemann-Hilbert problem associated with the equation.
result: Obtains long-time asymptotic expansion of the solution up to an optimal error order, proving asymptotic stability in the dispersive wave region.
conclusion: The solution is asymptotically stable under the given initial conditions, with improved generality of initial data.

title: TokaGrad: End-to-end Differentiable Tokamak Simulator For L-to-H Full Scenario Optimization
authors: Jaemin Seo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As fusion energy moves from theoretical feasibility toward commercialization, design of new reactor concepts, autonomous tokamak control, and high-performance scenario optimization are becoming increasingly important. Traditionally, such optimization tasks have relied on costly trial-and-error or brute-force parameter searches, based on black-box experiments or simulations. Recently, advances in differentiable programming are changing the paradigm of numerical simulation. Unlike conventional simulations, which are typically executed as locally connected step-by-step procedures, differentiable simulation represents the entire simulation pipeline as a connected computational graph. In such a framework, machine parameters, actuator waveforms, and plasma responses are linked through differentiable operations, allowing Jacobians to propagate across the full simulation. This enables direct gradient-based control and optimization using the internal sensitivities of the simulator, rather than treating the simulator as a black box. Here, we present TokaGrad, an end-to-end differentiable tokamak transport simulator for full-scenario modeling, including ramp-up, L-mode operation, and H-mode access. TokaGrad self-consistently integrates differentiable models for plasma equilibrium, transport, heating, L-H transition, and pedestal formation. To our knowledge, this is the first differentiable tokamak simulator capable of self-consistently modeling dynamic full-discharge scenarios where actuators and plasma evolve together with equilibrium, pedestal, and confinement-regime transitions. We demonstrate that, when coupled to gradient-based optimizers, TokaGrad enables reactor-design optimization, actuator control, and full-scenario waveform optimization. This framework provides a pathway toward automated, differentiable optimization of burning-plasma scenarios and reactor concepts.
tldr: This paper presents a differentiable tokamak simulator for fusion plasma scenario optimization, which is unrelated to quantum information theory or quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Fusion energy optimization traditionally relies on costly trial-and-error; differentiable programming offers a more efficient approach.
method: The authors develop TokaGrad, an end-to-end differentiable simulator integrating models for plasma equilibrium, transport, heating, L-H transition, and pedestal formation.
result: TokaGrad enables gradient-based optimization of reactor design, actuator control, and full-scenario waveforms.
conclusion: This framework provides a pathway toward automated, differentiable optimization of burning-plasma scenarios and reactor concepts.

title: I See You, Do You See Me? Perception-based Crowdedness And Behavioral Responses In Pedestrian Dynamics
authors: Pratik Mullick Igor Ho{\l}owacz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pedestrian traffic is commonly characterized using local density, yet the interactions experienced by individuals depend on the relative positions and perceptual relevance of surrounding pedestrians. This raises the question of whether behavioral relationships inferred from local crowdedness are robust to the representation of perceptual anisotropy, and how interaction geometry shapes pedestrian adaptation over time. We analyze experimental pedestrian crossing flows over angles from 0 to 180 degrees using a distance-weighted measure of local crowdedness. Perceptual anisotropy is varied by reducing the contribution of pedestrians outside the focal pedestrian's field of view. We examine the temporal evolution of crowdedness and its relationships with velocity, directional deviation, and acceleration. Anisotropy primarily changes the numerical scale of crowdedness, while the qualitative dynamics, temporal progression, and crossing-angle dependence remain largely preserved. Pedestrians deviate appreciably from their expected group directions, but changes between successive walking directions remain small, indicating adaptation through smooth, incremental corrections rather than abrupt turns. Acceleration dynamics reveal an asymmetry between disruption and recovery: initial deceleration varies strongly with crossing geometry, whereas recovery accelerations are more similar across angles. Non-retracing trajectories in the behavioral phase spaces show that similar instantaneous conditions can correspond to different phases of the interaction. Overall, interaction geometry has a stronger influence on the organization of crossing flows than the perceptual weighting used to quantify local crowdedness. More broadly, dynamic fundamental diagrams provide a more complete characterization of transient pedestrian interactions than conventional relationships based on instantaneous state variables alone.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: The Weighted Connected p-Median Problem
authors: Murat Elh\"useyni, Burak Kocuk, Mikl\'os Kr\'esz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The connected p-median problem is defined as a variant of the classical p-median problem when the facility nodes induce a connected subgraph. In this paper, we introduce the weighted version of the above problem when the weight of the facility connection in the objective function is defined by the minimum weight spanning tree of the facility nodes. This approach is motivated by the sink node selection in distributed sensor networks, in which the collected information is shared among the sink nodes through the minimum spanning tree. The weights of the graph determining the network topology of the candidate sink nodes as connection costs are distinguished from the standard access costs of the p-median problem. The fixed deployment costs for the setup of facilities are also considered. The objective is to minimize the overall cost as the sum of deployment cost, access cost and connection cost. We show that the problem is NP-hard and propose three mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulations adapted from the traveling salesperson problem literature. Since these formulations are poorly scalable with respect to network size, we develop a four-phase matheuristic method based on linear programming rounding. We conduct an extensive computational study to evaluate the performance of the MILP formulations and 22 variants of the matheuristic under different parameter settings. The results indicate that the MILP models perform effectively on small instances but struggle to solve medium- and large-scale instances within a two-hour time limit. In contrast, several matheuristic variants consistently produce high-quality solutions within minutes. Finally, we analyze the impact of network structure, size, density, and the parameter [MATH] on solution quality, providing further insights for network design.
tldr: This paper introduces a weighted connected p-median problem for facility location with connection costs defined by minimum spanning tree, motivated by sink node selection in sensor networks.
motivation: The problem arises from distributed sensor networks where sink nodes must be connected via a minimum spanning tree, and the goal is to minimize total deployment, access, and connection costs.
method: The authors prove NP-hardness, propose three MILP formulations adapted from TSP literature, and develop a four-phase matheuristic based on linear programming rounding.
result: MILP models work for small instances but fail for medium/large ones within two hours; the matheuristic produces high-quality solutions in minutes.
conclusion: The matheuristic is effective for practical network design, and the study provides insights into the impact of network structure and parameters.

title: Parallel Versions Of The Mesh Adaptive Direct Search Algorithm
authors: S\'ebastien Le Digabel, Antoine Lesage-Landry, Samuel Mendoza, Christophe Tribes
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work surveys the different parallel variants of the mesh adaptive direct search (MADS) algorithm for constrained blackbox optimization. These problems can inherently imply high computational costs due to the possible large number of variables and multi-modality of the search space. In addition, the potential time-intensive nature and time heterogeneity of the blackboxes defining the problem prompts the need for efficient implementations. Parallelism emerges as an actionable solution to mitigate computation time, as modern computer systems rely on multi-core architecture. The reviewed methods employ diverse levels of parallelism and distinct parallel strategies to effectively tackle each aspect outlined above. The manuscript details the practical implementations, provides computational results, and offers insights into the advantages and limitations of each MADS parallel method.
tldr: This paper surveys parallel variants of the mesh adaptive direct search algorithm for constrained blackbox optimization.
motivation: Blackbox optimization problems are computationally expensive, and parallelism can mitigate computation time on modern multi-core systems.
method: The authors review different parallel strategies for the MADS algorithm, detailing implementations and providing computational results.
result: The paper offers insights into the advantages and limitations of each parallel MADS method.
conclusion: Parallelism is an effective approach to speed up MADS, but the choice of strategy depends on the problem characteristics.

title: Integrability Of Cauchy Problems For Discrete Conformal Maps And Circle Patterns
authors: Anton Izosimov Maxim Arnold
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A map from a square lattice to the Riemann sphere is called discrete conformal if the image of every elementary square is a harmonic quadrilateral. We prove that the initial value problem for discrete conformal maps with quasi-periodic boundary conditions is Liouville integrable. We also show that the image of the embedding of Schramm's orthogonal square grid circle patterns into the space of discrete conformal maps is the real part of a symplectic leaf. As a consequence, we obtain the integrability of the corresponding Cauchy problem for circle patterns.
tldr: This paper proves the Liouville integrability of the Cauchy problem for discrete conformal maps and circle patterns.
motivation: To understand the integrability properties of discrete conformal maps and their connection to circle patterns.
method: The authors use symplectic geometry and the theory of integrable systems to analyze the initial value problem with quasi-periodic boundary conditions.
result: They show that the Cauchy problem for discrete conformal maps is Liouville integrable and that Schramm's circle patterns correspond to a symplectic leaf.
conclusion: The work establishes a rigorous integrability framework for discrete conformal geometry, with implications for circle patterns.

title: Construction And Optimization Of Summation-by-Parts Operators For General Function Spaces Using An Improved Generalized Gaussian Quadrature Algorithm
authors: Alex Bercik, Lisa Patrascu, David W. Zingg
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct optimized summation-by-parts (SBP) operators for general function spaces with provably minimal degrees of freedom on open, closed, and half-open nodal distributions. These operators rely on generalized Gaussian quadrature rules, for which we present an improved algorithm that is flexible, efficient, and provably convergent. In cases where free parameters are available, we further introduce two operator optimization strategies. We test our operators on a handful of numerical examples that contain large or unbounded gradients, in which some a priori knowledge of the solution has been assumed to select an appropriate basis. The novel operators are found to outperform standard polynomial operators by several orders of magnitude in solution accuracy relative to degrees of freedom. Furthermore, our novel operators significantly outperform function-space SBP operators with equispaced nodal distributions, which require significantly more nodes for the same operator basis. Finally, we demonstrate that the operator optimization procedures are critical to achieving accurate and efficient discretizations, as the standard SBP construction procedure can lead to nullspace-inconsistent and poorly-conditioned operators.
tldr: This paper presents a method for constructing and optimizing summation-by-parts operators for general function spaces using an improved generalized Gaussian quadrature algorithm, with applications in numerical analysis.
motivation: Summation-by-parts operators are important for stable and accurate discretizations of partial differential equations, but existing constructions are limited to polynomial spaces or require many nodes.
method: The authors develop an improved algorithm for generalized Gaussian quadrature that is flexible, efficient, and provably convergent, and use it to construct SBP operators with minimal degrees of freedom. They also introduce two optimization strategies for free parameters.
result: The novel operators outperform standard polynomial operators by orders of magnitude in solution accuracy relative to degrees of freedom, and significantly outperform function-space SBP operators with equispaced nodal distributions.
conclusion: The optimized SBP operators are critical for accurate and efficient discretizations, and the construction procedure is generalizable to various function spaces.

title: Polynomial Matrices In Integer Programming With Restricted Subdeterminants
authors: Marcel Celaya, Stefan Kuhlmann, Robert Weismantel
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a framework for tackling questions in discrete optimization associated with parametric constraint matrices. More precisely, the constraint matrices have entries that are polynomials in one variable and all subdeterminants of these matrices are polynomials in a given prescribed set [MATH]. Two key problems arise in this context. The first is the recognition problem: can a matrix of this form be recognized in polynomial time? The second is the optimization problem: given an integer program whose constraint matrix is of this form, can it be solved in polynomial time? We answer both questions affirmatively for a particular set [MATH] consisting of nine linear forms. The matrices we consider are of themselves independent interest; they arise as matrix projections of certain bimodular matrices that admit two distinct unimodular projections.
tldr: This paper studies polynomial matrices with restricted subdeterminants for integer programming, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: The paper aims to solve recognition and optimization problems for integer programs with parametric constraint matrices whose subdeterminants are restricted to a prescribed set.
method: The authors introduce a framework for polynomial matrices and show that for a specific set of nine linear forms, both recognition and optimization can be done in polynomial time.
result: They answer both the recognition and optimization problems affirmatively for the considered set of subdeterminants.
conclusion: The work contributes to discrete optimization but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Tensor-Train Discontinuous Galerkin Method For The Vlasov-Maxwell System
authors: Rujeko Chinomona, Dibyendu Adak, William J. Barham, Duc P. Truong, Nathan V. Roberts, Kim {\O}. Rasmussen, Boian S. Alexandrov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a tensor-train discontinuous Galerkin (TT-DG) formulation for the Vlasov--Maxwell system that combines a modal DG discretization with low-rank tensor representations of the phase-space solution and discrete operators. The formulation exploits the tensor-product structure of the DG discretization to perform quadrature, differentiation, nonlinear upwind flux evaluation, and time integration directly in compressed form. The method is evaluated on several standard 1D2V Vlasov--Maxwell benchmark problems, including the streaming Weibel instability, weak Landau damping, and two-stream instability problems. Across these problems, the TT formulation reproduces the accuracy and conservation behavior of the underlying full-grid DG discretization while substantially reducing memory usage and runtime. For weakly nonlinear problems, compression ratios exceeding [MATH] are obtained together with significant speedups relative to the full-grid solver. For the strongly nonlinear two-stream instability problem, the TT formulation remains effective despite reduced compressibility caused by fine-scale phase-space filamentation. These results demonstrate that tensor-train representations provide an effective approach for reducing the computational cost of deterministic DG-based kinetic plasma simulations while retaining the favorable numerical properties of the underlying discretization.
tldr: This paper presents a tensor-train discontinuous Galerkin method for the Vlasov-Maxwell system, focusing on computational efficiency for kinetic plasma simulations.
motivation: Kinetic plasma simulations using the Vlasov-Maxwell system are computationally expensive due to high-dimensional phase space; the authors aim to reduce memory and runtime via low-rank tensor representations.
method: A modal discontinuous Galerkin discretization is combined with tensor-train decompositions to represent the phase-space solution and operators in compressed form, enabling quadrature, differentiation, and time integration directly in the compressed format.
result: The method achieves compression ratios exceeding 10^5 and significant speedups on benchmark problems (Weibel instability, Landau damping, two-stream instability) while preserving accuracy and conservation properties of the full-grid solver.
conclusion: Tensor-train representations effectively reduce computational cost for deterministic DG-based kinetic plasma simulations, especially for weakly nonlinear problems, though strong nonlinearity reduces compressibility.

title: Nonconvex Composite Functional Constraints Via First-Order Augmented Lagrangian Methods Under Local Regularity
authors: Jiajin Li Linglingzhi Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study nonasymptotic convergence of primal-dual methods for a class of nonconvex constrained optimization problems with a convex-composite structure. In this class, both the objective and the functional inequality constraints are given by convex Lipschitz outer functions composed with smooth nonlinear inner mappings. The analysis is complicated by constraint violation in a nonconvex functional inequality system and by the lack of an a priori bound on the multipliers. To address these issues, we restrict the dual variable to an auxiliary compact set and analyze a smoothed prox-linear augmented Lagrangian method through a nonsmooth nonconvex-concave minimax reformulation. The main contribution is a finite-time mechanism for converting stationarity of the truncated minimax problem into a KKT certificate for the original constrained problem. We show that, for a sufficiently large penalty parameter, all but a controlled number of iterates enter a near-feasible region. On this region, a local conic regularity condition uniformly bounds the associated prox-linear multipliers and thereby makes the artificial dual truncation inactive at the selected iterates. Building on this mechanism, we establish explicit convergence rates for the proposed method in terms of the KKT residual. With dual regularization, a global dual error bound together with a bias-balancing argument gives an [MATH] rate. In the unregularized case, under additional local structural assumptions including piecewise linearity of the outer functions, a local dual error bound yields the sharper [MATH] rate.
tldr: This paper studies nonconvex composite functional constraints optimization using first-order augmented Lagrangian methods, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper addresses convergence of primal-dual methods for nonconvex constrained optimization with convex-composite structure, which is a topic in optimization theory.
method: The authors propose a smoothed prox-linear augmented Lagrangian method and analyze its convergence via a nonsmooth nonconvex-concave minimax reformulation, using local conic regularity and dual error bounds.
result: They establish explicit convergence rates for the KKT residual, achieving O(1/√k) rate with dual regularization and O(1/k) rate under additional structural assumptions.
conclusion: The work provides finite-time guarantees for obtaining KKT points in nonconvex composite optimization, but is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A Linearized And Structure-preserving Mixed Virtual Element Method For The Extended Fisher-Kolmogorov Equation
authors: Zhen Guan, Xianxian Cao, Houchao Zhang, Junjun Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In thsi paper, based on the leap-frog discretization in time and the mixed virtual element discretization in space, we developed a linearized and structure-preserving numerical algorithm. The main contributions of this work lie in that we not only provide a rigorous proof of the energy dissipation property of the fully discrete numerical scheme, but also establish the unconditionally optimal convergence analysis by means of a inverse inequality. The core of the proof lies in the classified discussion of the relationship between \(\tau\) and [MATH]. Finally, two numerical examples are provided to validate the correctness of the theoretical analysis as well as the energy dissipation property of the proposed scheme.
tldr: This paper develops a linearized and structure-preserving mixed virtual element method for the extended Fisher-Kolmogorov equation.
motivation: To design an efficient numerical scheme that preserves energy dissipation and achieves optimal convergence for the extended Fisher-Kolmogorov equation.
method: Uses leap-frog time discretization and mixed virtual element spatial discretization, with rigorous proof of energy dissipation and optimal convergence via an inverse inequality.
result: Establishes unconditional optimal convergence and energy dissipation property of the fully discrete scheme, validated by numerical examples.
conclusion: The proposed method is effective for solving the extended Fisher-Kolmogorov equation while preserving its energy structure.

title: Solving Stochastic Fixed-Point Equations With High Probability
authors: Jelena Diakonikolas
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study stochastic fixed-point equations [MATH] over normed spaces [MATH], where the operator [MATH] is nonexpansive or contractive and is accessed only through unbiased stochastic evaluations with bounded second central moment. Given [MATH], the goal is to output [MATH] such that [MATH] with probability at least [MATH]. We introduce VR-GHAL, a variance-reduced gradual Halpern method for quadratically smoothable Banach spaces. The key algorithmic ingredient is a recursive stochastic estimator based on clipped differences of oracle evaluations: instead of clipping [MATH] itself, we clip stochastic differences at the Lipschitz scale [MATH]. This makes the estimator pathwise Lipschitz along the algorithmic trajectory while permitting martingale concentration under finite second moments in the native norm. Our main theorem gives an anytime high-probability residual bound: on a single event of probability at least [MATH], the residual decreases nearly geometrically across epochs, up to lower-order logarithmic factors. motivation: The paper addresses the problem of solving stochastic fixed-point equations with high probability, which is a topic in optimization and stochastic approximation.
method: The authors introduce VR-GHAL, a variance-reduced gradual Halpern method that uses a recursive stochastic estimator based on clipped differences of oracle evaluations.
result: The main theorem provides an anytime high-probability residual bound with oracle complexity depending on target error and Lipschitz constant.
conclusion: The method achieves high-probability convergence under bounded variance and improves rates under stronger oracle assumptions.

title: Functions And Means Of Accretive Operators
authors: Mitsuru Uchiyama
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a bounded accretive operator on a Hilbert space and [MATH] an operator monotone function on [MATH] with [MATH]. Then, for [MATH], analytic function [MATH] is defined by Riesz-Dunford integral. method: Uses Riesz-Dunford integral and norm limits to define analytic functions of accretive operators.
