title: Optimal Finite Element Error Estimates And Newton Convergence For A Quasilinear Elliptic Problem With Mixed Boundary Conditions
authors: Mihai Bucataru
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The article studies finite element approximations of a quasilinear elliptic heat-conduction problem with inhomogeneous mixed boundary conditions. The conductivity tensor is matrix-valued, anisotropic, possibly nonsymmetric, and dependent on both position and temperature, rendering the problem nonlinear, nonmonotone, and nonpotential. The nonlinear algebraic system arising from the Galerkin discretization is solved using Newton's method, with a posteriori guarantees provided by a computable Newton-Kantorovich criterion and a mesh-dependent stopping rule that ensures that the algebraic error is asymptotically negligible relative to the discretization error. Since the discrete solution need not be unique, we prove that every discrete solution satisfies the optimal convergence rates. The analysis combines mixed-boundary elliptic regularity with an Aubin-Nitsche duality argument adapted to the quasilinear setting. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions confirm the predicted convergence rates and demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed criterion.
tldr: This paper studies finite element error estimates and Newton convergence for a quasilinear elliptic heat-conduction problem with mixed boundary conditions.
motivation: The paper aims to provide optimal convergence rates for finite element approximations of a nonlinear, nonmonotone, nonpotential elliptic problem, which is a classical numerical analysis topic.
method: The analysis combines mixed-boundary elliptic regularity with an Aubin-Nitsche duality argument adapted to the quasilinear setting, and uses a Newton-Kantorovich criterion for algebraic error control.
result: It proves that every discrete solution achieves optimal convergence rates, and numerical experiments in 2D and 3D confirm the predicted rates.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous error estimates and a practical stopping criterion for Newton's method in this class of problems.

title: Polyhedral Extended Formulations That Approximate The Gomory Closure For Packing Problems
authors: Friedrich Eisenbrand, Samuel Fiorini, Lars Rohwedder, Jiaye Wei
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider [MATH] packing problems [MATH], with [MATH]. A way to solve such problems is via tightening the linear programming relaxation [MATH] with Gomory . The Gomory-closure [MATH] of [MATH] is the intersection of [MATH] with all its cutting planes. The optimization problem over [MATH] is NP-hard. Mastrolilli (2020) has shown that for fixed [MATH], the Lasserre hierarchy yields a polynomial-size convex but non-polyhedral extended formulation that approximates [MATH] up to a factor of [MATH]. Our main result is the construction of a polyhedral and polynomial extended formulation that approximates [MATH] with the same approximation guarantee. Our construction is based on first principles. Like Mastrolilli's approach, ours also applies to higher iterates [MATH] for fixed [MATH] and [MATH]. In contrast to an explicit construction, communication complexity provides an alternative way to describe extended formulations. Using this approach we obtain a quasi-polynomial polyhedral extended formulation for the above problem that is superior in some parameter regimes. To achieve this, we describe a communication protocol extending Yannakakis' protocol to decide whether the clique of Alice and the stable set of Bob intersect.
tldr: This paper presents polyhedral extended formulations that approximate the Gomory closure for packing problems, a topic in combinatorial optimization.
motivation: The Gomory closure is a powerful tool for solving integer programming problems, but optimizing over it is NP-hard. The authors aim to construct polynomial-size polyhedral extended formulations that approximate the closure.
method: The authors construct a polyhedral extended formulation based on first principles, and also use communication complexity to obtain a quasi-polynomial formulation.
result: They achieve a polynomial-size polyhedral extended formulation that approximates the Gomory closure with the same approximation guarantee as Mastrolilli's Lasserre hierarchy approach.
conclusion: The work provides a polyhedral alternative to the non-polyhedral Lasserre hierarchy for approximating the Gomory closure, with potential applications in integer programming.

title: A General Framework For Nonlocal Traffic Flow Models On Networks
authors: Alexander Keimer, Lukas Pflug, Florian Prohaska
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09227v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a general computational framework for macroscopic nonlocal traffic flow models on networks with multiple commodities. The model combines scalar conservation laws on edges with nonlocal velocity functions and couples them via buffer-based junction dynamics. Routing is defined in general as a prescription for distributing drivers across outgoing road segments. As an example, we implement dynamic k-shortest-path routing, where travel times along roads and waiting times at intersections are used to compute shortest paths to the commodities' destinations at each time step, and drivers are distributed accordingly. In another example, we optimize routing over a considered time horizon to minimize the total travel time. This framework naturally creates a feedback loop between traffic evolution and route choice. Numerical examples, ranging from small test cases to large grid-like networks, demonstrate the robustness of the approach and allow for a comparison of different routing strategies.
tldr: This paper presents a computational framework for macroscopic nonlocal traffic flow models on networks, focusing on routing and traffic evolution.
motivation: To develop a general framework for modeling nonlocal traffic flow on networks with multiple commodities and dynamic routing.
method: The framework uses scalar conservation laws on edges with nonlocal velocity functions, coupled via buffer-based junction dynamics, and implements dynamic k-shortest-path routing and optimization over a time horizon.
result: Numerical examples demonstrate robustness and allow comparison of different routing strategies on test cases and large grid-like networks.
conclusion: The framework effectively models traffic flow with feedback between traffic evolution and route choice, enabling analysis of various routing strategies.

title: Central Limit Theorems For Functionals Of Persistence Diagrams In Germ-Grain Random Set Models With Applications To Goodness-of-Fit Testing
authors: Marcela Mandari\'c Vesna Gotovac {\dj}oga\v{s}
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper establishes a central limit theorem (CLT) for functionals of [MATH]-bounded persistence diagrams arising from germ-grain random set models. Building on stabilisation methods for marked point processes, we show that, under certain conditions, these topological summaries exhibit asymptotic normality as the observation window increases, particularly for models with exponential decay of correlations. These results are applied in goodness-of-fit tests designed to detect spatial interactions such as clustering or repulsion. Using test statistics derived from rectangular partitions of persistence diagrams and functional summaries (e.g., the APF or the support function of the lift zonoid), the study distinguishes between different models. Finally, the methodology is applied to histological images of breast tissue.
tldr: This paper proves central limit theorems for persistence diagram functionals in germ-grain random set models and applies them to goodness-of-fit testing for spatial interactions.
motivation: Persistence diagrams are used in topological data analysis, but their asymptotic distribution is not well understood for random set models. The authors aim to provide a CLT to enable statistical inference.
method: The paper uses stabilisation methods for marked point processes to establish asymptotic normality of functionals of persistence diagrams under exponential decay of correlations. Test statistics are derived from rectangular partitions and functional summaries like the APF or lift zonoid.
result: Central limit theorems are proven for bounded persistence diagrams in germ-grain models, and the methodology is applied to distinguish clustering vs. repulsion in spatial point patterns, with a case study on breast tissue images.
conclusion: The CLT enables goodness-of-fit tests for spatial interactions, demonstrating practical utility in histology image analysis.

title: Approximation By Quasi-projection Operators And Dual Wavelet Frames In Sobolev Spaces
authors: Aleksandr Krivoshein Danila Kotov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a quasi-projection operator [MATH] formed by a compactly supported function [MATH] and a compactly supported distribution [MATH] with dilation matrix [MATH], we establish necessary and sufficient conditions under which it provides prescribed simultaneous approximation and simultaneous density orders for a function [MATH] from the Sobolev space [MATH] and for its derivatives. The obtained criteria are then used to endow MRA-based dual wavelet frames in a pair of dual Sobolev spaces with the desired simultaneous approximation properties.
tldr: This paper studies approximation properties of quasi-projection operators and dual wavelet frames in Sobolev spaces.
motivation: To establish necessary and sufficient conditions for quasi-projection operators to provide prescribed simultaneous approximation orders for functions and their derivatives in Sobolev spaces.
method: The authors analyze quasi-projection operators formed by a compactly supported function and a compactly supported distribution with dilation matrix, and use the criteria to construct MRA-based dual wavelet frames with desired approximation properties.
result: Necessary and sufficient conditions for simultaneous approximation and density orders are derived, and applied to dual wavelet frames in Sobolev spaces.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for approximation in Sobolev spaces using quasi-projection operators and dual wavelet frames, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fifth-Order Well-Balanced Path-Conservative A-weno Scheme For The Ripa Model
authors: Yan-Ping Qiu, Zhen Gao, Alexander Kurganov, Bao-Shan Wang, Xiao Wen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we introduce a fifth-order well-balanced (WB) path-conservative A-WENO scheme with the central-upwind numerical fluxes (PCCU-5) for the Ripa model. The proposed scheme is capable of exactly preserving a variety of steady states, including still-water, moving-water, isobaric, and constant water height ones. This goal is achieved with the help of a flux globalization technique: The source terms are incorporated into the fluxes, resulting in a quasi-conservative system, for which central-upwind numerical fluxes are computed using the path-conservative integration. The proposed A-WENO scheme utilizes a WENO interpolation of the equilibrium variables rather than the conservative ones to ensure the WB property. In addition, we perform the WENO interpolation of the local characteristic equilibrium variables to mitigate numerical oscillations near discontinuities. We perform a series of numerical experiments, which demonstrate that the proposed fifth-order WB PCCU-5 scheme achieves high resolution and clearly outperforms its second-order counterpart. Our numerical results also demonstrate the importance of the local characteristic projection for significantly reducing (eliminating) numerical oscillations near discontinuities.
tldr: This paper presents a fifth-order well-balanced path-conservative A-WENO scheme for the Ripa model, a system of hyperbolic conservation laws used in geophysical fluid dynamics.
motivation: The Ripa model requires numerical schemes that preserve steady states and handle discontinuities without oscillations, which is challenging for high-order methods.
method: The authors develop a fifth-order A-WENO scheme using a flux globalization technique to incorporate source terms into fluxes, and employ WENO interpolation on equilibrium variables with local characteristic projection to suppress oscillations.
result: Numerical experiments show the scheme exactly preserves multiple steady states and achieves high resolution, outperforming its second-order counterpart and reducing oscillations near discontinuities.
conclusion: The proposed scheme is effective for simulating the Ripa model with high accuracy and stability, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: On Incremental Design Of Large-Scale Networks Of Nondeterministic Metric Finite State Systems
authors: Giordano Pola
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we address control design of Networks of nondeterministic and metric finite state Systems (NoS) where some systems are plants, others act as controllers, and some are uncontrolled processes. The control architecture of NoS extends decentralized control architectures. The problem addressed consists in designing local controllers for enforcing on the corresponding plants, local specifications given by regular languages over plants' state alphabet, up to desired accuracies. The approach used to solve the problem is termed incremental and consists in finding solutions on an increasing sequence of NoS extracted from the original NoS.
tldr: This paper addresses control design for networks of nondeterministic metric finite state systems using an incremental approach.
motivation: The authors aim to design local controllers for enforcing local specifications on plants within a network, extending decentralized control architectures.
method: An incremental design method is proposed that finds solutions on an increasing sequence of networks extracted from the original network.
result: The paper presents a method for incremental control design but does not provide experimental or theoretical results relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.
conclusion: The work is in control theory and does not align with any of the specified research directions.

title: Multi-type Galton-Watson Processes In Dynamical Environments
authors: Thomas Morand
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define a model of multi-type Galton-Watson processes in dynamical environments where the environment evolves according to a dynamical system (X,T). Three behaviours are possible: uniformly subcritical, critical, and uniformly supercritical. We provide a criterion to determine the regime of a multi-type Galton-Watson process in dynamical environments. We study the continuity of the probability of extinction q in the uniformly supercritical case.
tldr: This paper studies multi-type Galton-Watson processes in dynamical environments, focusing on extinction probabilities and regime classification.
motivation: To understand branching processes in environments that evolve deterministically, extending classical Galton-Watson theory.
method: The authors define a model where the environment evolves according to a dynamical system and analyze the process using ergodic theory and branching process techniques.
result: A criterion is provided to determine whether the process is uniformly subcritical, critical, or uniformly supercritical, and continuity of the extinction probability is studied in the supercritical case.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of branching processes in varying environments but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: The Cost Of Discretization In Functional Linear Regression: Minimax Rates And Adaptation
authors: Yicheng Li T. Tony Cai
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study scalar-on-function linear regression when each covariate curve is observed only through finitely many noisy point evaluations. Our goal is to characterize the minimax estimation and prediction risks as joint functions of the number of trajectories [MATH] and the within-trajectory resolution [MATH]. Working in a fixed trigonometric eigenbasis, with covariance eigenvalues decaying at rate [MATH] and slope function of Sobolev smoothness [MATH], we derive matching minimax upper and lower bounds under two canonical sampling schemes. Under an independent random design, the minimax prediction rate is [MATH]. The first term is the fully observed functional linear regression benchmark, while the second term captures the cost of noisy point evaluations after amplification by the inverse covariance operator. Under a common design on an equally spaced grid, the shared sampling geometry introduces additional obstructions, and the minimax prediction rate becomes [MATH]. Here the third term represents discretization error induced by the fixed grid, whereas the fourth reflects the cost of identifying unknown eigenvalues from observations on a common grid. We further construct data-driven adaptive estimators that screen the covariance scale and threshold blockwise prediction energy, attaining these rates without prior knowledge of the eigenvalue sequence or the smoothness indices. The results reveal a sharp phase transition that depends on the sampling resolution under independent design and a richer phase diagram under common design. Numerical simulations and a real data example illustrate the theoretical findings.
tldr: This paper studies minimax estimation and prediction rates in functional linear regression with discretely observed noisy curves.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits of regression when covariates are observed only through noisy point evaluations is important for practical statistical inference.
method: The authors derive matching minimax upper and lower bounds under independent random design and common fixed grid design, using a trigonometric eigenbasis and Sobolev smoothness assumptions.
result: Minimax prediction rates are characterized, revealing phase transitions and additional costs due to discretization and eigenvalue estimation under common design.
conclusion: The results provide a complete theoretical picture of the cost of discretization in functional linear regression, with adaptive estimators achieving optimal rates.

title: $\mathrm{IP}_{\mathrm{rat}}$-polynomial Recurrence And Large Intersections
authors: Or Shalom Borys Holikov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09358v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a rationally independent sequence of integer valued nonlinear polynomials. We show that for all [MATH], every Folner sequence [MATH], and every [MATH], the set $[MATH]$ intersects every IP generated by a sequence with rational spectrum. Our methods involve the study of the characteristic factors for multiple ergodic polynomial averages along IPs. In particular, we also prove a pointwise convergence theorem for polynomial averages along IPs with rational spectrum, generalizing a well known result of Leibman.
tldr: This paper proves that for rationally independent nonlinear integer-valued polynomials, certain sets intersect every IP set with rational spectrum, using ergodic theory and polynomial recurrence.
motivation: To understand recurrence properties of polynomial sequences and their intersections with IP sets, which is a problem in ergodic theory and combinatorial number theory.
method: The authors study characteristic factors for multiple ergodic polynomial averages along IPs and prove a pointwise convergence theorem for polynomial averages along IPs with rational spectrum.
result: For any rationally independent sequence of integer-valued nonlinear polynomials, the set of return times intersects every IP set generated by a sequence with rational spectrum.
conclusion: The work generalizes a known result of Leibman and contributes to the theory of polynomial recurrence and IP sets.

title: On A Conjecture About Schauder-Basis Properties Of The Daubechies Wavelet Packets
authors: Morten Nielsen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nielsen and Zhou (, ACHA 13 (2002), 22--34) conjectured that for every Daubechies filter of length at least four the associated wavelet packets fail to be a Schauder basis of [MATH] for every [MATH]; their own [MATH] estimate only reaches extreme exponents. We prove the Schauder-basis-failure half of the conjecture in full, for every [MATH] with [MATH], in the length-four case. The proof combines convexity of the wavelet packet pressure function with the uniqueness of equilibrium states for irreducible matrix families due to Feng and K\"aenm\"aki (2011) and an exact algebraic separation of two periodic spectral growth rates of the high-pass transition matrices.
tldr: This paper proves a conjecture about Schauder-basis properties of Daubechies wavelet packets, a topic in harmonic analysis and wavelet theory.
motivation: The conjecture concerns whether Daubechies wavelet packets form a Schauder basis for Lp spaces; previous results only covered extreme exponents.
method: The proof combines convexity of the wavelet packet pressure function with uniqueness of equilibrium states for irreducible matrix families and an algebraic separation of spectral growth rates.
result: The Schauder-basis-failure half of the conjecture is proven for all p≠2 in the length-four case.
conclusion: The result confirms the conjecture for the length-four Daubechies filter, but the general case remains open.

title: Centers Of q-Schur Algebras
authors: Xirui Yu Jian Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a direct BLM-coordinate description of the centers of generic [MATH]-Schur algebras for type [MATH] and type [MATH]. For the [MATH]-Schur algebras [MATH] of type [MATH], we show that any central element is supported on some matrices satisfying certain balance properties, and that its coefficients are precisely the solutions of an explicit finite linear system derived from the left and right multiplication formulas for the Chevalley generators of [MATH]. This yields an effective reduced row echelon form construction of a [MATH]-basis of the center, a basis that we then compare with the central bases obtained by Fu via quantum Schur-Weyl duality. For the [MATH]-Schur algebras [MATH] of type [MATH], we first apply a method similar to that for type [MATH] to provide a basis for the center. In addition, we provide another structural description of the center by decomposing [MATH] into the [MATH]-Schur algebras of type [MATH], and these two descriptions are compatible. The center of a variant [MATH] of [MATH] is also discussed.
tldr: This paper studies the centers of q-Schur algebras using BLM coordinates and linear systems, with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: The authors aim to describe the centers of q-Schur algebras for types A and D, which is a purely algebraic problem.
method: They use BLM-coordinate descriptions and solve linear systems derived from Chevalley generators to construct bases for the centers.
result: They provide explicit bases for the centers of generic q-Schur algebras and compare them with known bases from quantum Schur-Weyl duality.
conclusion: The work contributes to representation theory and quantum groups, but has no relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Full Cross-correlation Inversion For Quantitative Passive Imaging With Time-harmonic Acoustic Waves
authors: Florian Faucher Jean Dutheil
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the inverse problem for the quantitative reconstruction of physical properties in the context of passive imaging, where ambient wavefields are used to infer a medium. The data are modeled as a superposition of waves generated by stochastic sources. In this work, we focus on time-harmonic acoustic wave propagation and assume that the stochastic sources exciting the medium are zero-mean and spatially uncorrelated. Under these assumptions, the expected value of the cross-correlation between signals recorded at two locations can be related to the deterministic Green's function and the covariance of the source terms. We follow a first-order formulation of the wave equation, which enables the treatment of correlations between different types of wavefields. A numerical framework is developed for the resulting nonlinear inverse problem. The quantitative reconstruction is carried out using an iterative minimization scheme, in which the gradient of the misfit functional is computed via the adjoint-state method. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions are performed using synthetic data, and inversions based on the expected value of cross-correlations are compared with those relying on direct wavefield measurements from active-source acquisitions.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical framework for quantitative passive imaging using time-harmonic acoustic waves and cross-correlation inversion.
motivation: Passive imaging using ambient wavefields is desirable when active sources are unavailable, but quantitative reconstruction from cross-correlations is challenging.
method: The authors model data as superposition of waves from stochastic sources, relate cross-correlation to Green's function, and solve the nonlinear inverse problem via iterative minimization with adjoint-state gradient computation.
result: Numerical experiments in 2D and 3D demonstrate that cross-correlation inversion can achieve comparable reconstructions to active-source acquisitions.
conclusion: The proposed method enables quantitative passive imaging without active sources, with potential applications in geophysics and medical imaging.

title: Convex Relaxations For The Optimization Of Markov Processes
authors: Hongyi Zhang, Yuehaw Khoo, Tianyun Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of optimizing Markov processes that interpolate between two prescribed probability distributions while minimizing a given cost. The main computational challenge is the curse of dimensionality: in high-dimensional state spaces, representing the full distribution is intractable. To address this, we reformulate the problem in terms of sequential couplings and develop convex relaxations based on local marginals and cluster moments. These relaxations exploit locality and sparse interaction structure, provide computable lower bounds, and recover low-order statistics of the intermediate laws. We identify dynamic optimal transport as a special case of our Markov process optimization problem and develop a procedure for recovering the underlying Benamou--Brenier dynamics from the relaxed solution. We also show that the procedure extends to more general Markov processes and illustrate it with a constrained process between Ising models.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: The Continuous Relaxation Of Sparse Pca Is NP-hard
authors: Yong Xia Linbin Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Maximizing a symmetric quadratic form under simultaneous L1 norm inequality and L2 norm equality constraints is a standard and widely used continuous relaxation for Sparse Principal Component Analysis (SPCA). This paper settles the computational complexity of this continuous formulation by proving it is NP-hard. Furthermore, the variant with both L1 and L2 norm inequalities is also shown to be NP-hard.
tldr: This paper proves that the continuous relaxation of sparse PCA is NP-hard.
motivation: Sparse PCA is a widely used dimensionality reduction technique, and its continuous relaxation is a standard optimization problem. Understanding its computational complexity is important for algorithm design.
method: The authors prove NP-hardness by reducing from a known NP-hard problem, showing that maximizing a symmetric quadratic form under L1 norm inequality and L2 norm equality constraints is NP-hard.
result: Both the standard continuous relaxation and its variant with L1 and L2 norm inequalities are proven NP-hard.
conclusion: The continuous relaxation of sparse PCA is computationally intractable in general, implying that exact solutions are unlikely to be found efficiently.

title: Pre/Post-Assessment Cycles In Calculus: Supporting Student Preparation, Reflection, And Learning
authors: Chamila Malagoda Gamage
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article describes a semester-long implementation of pre/post-assessment cycles in an undergraduate Calculus I course. The activity was designed to address a common difficulty in lower-division mathematics courses: students often enter a new unit without knowing which prior ideas are relevant, which concepts deserve special attention, or how to judge their own progress before high-stakes exams. Brief pre-assessments were administered before major course units, and related post-assessment questions revisited key ideas after instruction. Students also completed short reflection prompts about what they learned, what remained challenging, and how their understanding changed. The paper analyzes student performance data, participation patterns, and reflective responses to examine how these cycles supported preparation, reflection, and learning. The study contributes a practical model for embedding low-stakes assessment and reflection into the regular structure of an undergraduate mathematics course.
tldr: This paper describes a pedagogical intervention using pre/post-assessment cycles in an undergraduate Calculus I course to improve student preparation, reflection, and learning.
motivation: Students in lower-division mathematics courses often lack awareness of relevant prior knowledge and struggle to self-assess their progress before exams.
method: Brief pre-assessments were administered before major units, followed by post-assessment questions and reflection prompts; student performance and participation data were analyzed.
result: The study provides a practical model for embedding low-stakes assessment and reflection into regular course structure, with analysis of student performance and reflective responses.
conclusion: Pre/post-assessment cycles can support student preparation and learning in undergraduate mathematics courses.

title: Fast-Track Ode: A Flipped, Game-Based Summer Differential Equations Course
authors: Chamila Malagoda Gamage
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article describes the implementation of a flipped, interactive, and game-based instructional design in an Elementary Differential Equations course taught during a six-week summer session. The course used real-time feedback, technology-supported visualization, collaborative problem solving, and mathematical games to support engagement, participation, and understanding in a fast-paced learning environment.
tldr: This paper describes a flipped, game-based instructional design for a summer differential equations course.
motivation: To improve engagement and understanding in a fast-paced summer course using interactive methods.
method: Implemented flipped classroom, real-time feedback, technology visualization, collaborative problem solving, and mathematical games.
result: The course design supported engagement, participation, and understanding in a six-week summer session.
conclusion: Game-based and flipped approaches can be effective for teaching differential equations in accelerated formats.

title: Inertial Forward-backward Algorithm With Exterior Penalization And Tikhonov Regularization
authors: Siqi Qu, Juan Peypouquet, Mathias Staudigl
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a real Hilbertian setting, we develop in this paper numerical splitting techniques guaranteeing strong convergence to the least norm solution of constrained variational inequalities. We develop a multiscale inertial forward-backward splitting algorithm for solving constrained monotone inclusion problems with multiscale penalization and vanishing Tikhonov regularization. The proposed framework accommodates smooth, nonsmooth, and mixed smooth--nonsmooth penalty operators, providing a unified treatment of a broad class of constrained monotone inclusion problems. In this general framework, we establish weak convergence of the generated iterates. By introducing a discrete Tikhonov central path, we further prove strong convergence to the minimum-norm solution of the problem under a mild constraint qualification condition on the problem data.
tldr: This paper develops an inertial forward-backward algorithm with exterior penalization and Tikhonov regularization for solving constrained monotone inclusion problems in Hilbert spaces.
motivation: The goal is to achieve strong convergence to the minimum-norm solution of constrained variational inequalities, which is important in optimization but not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors propose a multiscale inertial forward-backward splitting algorithm that incorporates exterior penalization and vanishing Tikhonov regularization, accommodating smooth, nonsmooth, and mixed penalty operators.
result: Weak convergence of the iterates is established, and strong convergence to the minimum-norm solution is proved under a mild constraint qualification condition using a discrete Tikhonov central path.
conclusion: The algorithm provides a unified numerical framework for constrained monotone inclusion problems, but the paper is purely in optimization and does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Entropy Bootstrapping For Wireless Embedded Systems
authors: Javier Blanco-Romero, Florina Almenares Mendoza, Daniel D\'iaz-S\'anchez, Andr\'es Mar\'in-L\'opez
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Weak randomness has broken deployed cryptography through implementation bugs, boot entropy scarcity, and backdoored generators. Inexpensive wireless sensors concentrate the risk because many boot or operate in highly deterministic conditions while relying on basic, rudimentary, or opaque RNGs. On ESP32-class boards, RF-disabled wireless device RNG register (WDEV) output is pseudorandom by specification yet passes the same statistical screens as RF-active states, showing that output tests cannot replace source-state admission. We propose a defense-in-depth boot path for ESP32-class IoT nodes that combines SRAM startup material, radio burst extraction, and asymmetric entropy capsules under explicit source-state admission. In radio burst extraction, a trusted node in the local IoT network, such as a gateway or dedicated entropy node, sends a public packet burst to open a measurement window. The client samples its own WDEV output and packet timing during that window, then credits only the local response. Capsules cover the cold-start case with a pre-provisioned asymmetric key pair. The trusted node encrypts fresh seed material to the client's public key and signs the capsule; the client verifies, decapsulates, and hashes before it has local entropy. We benchmark the ESP32 RNG under several radio operating modes, the fixed-burst extraction window, the deterministic capsule client path, and SRAM startup reads. Together, these measurements support an admission policy in which each root is credited only when its required source state and protocol checks hold.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: Offline Nash Solvers Meet Online Tree Search In Multi-Agent Games On Graphs
authors: Mukesh Kumar, Yue Guan, Panagiotis Tsiotras
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08892v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computing Nash equilibrium policies in multi-agent Pursuit-Evasion games (PEG) is challenging due to the exponential growth of the joint state and action spaces with the number of agents. Existing approaches either rely on offline equilibrium approximations, which may lack adaptability during execution, or online planning methods, which suffer from large branching factors. In this work, we propose Primitive-Guided Tree Search (PGTS), a hybrid framework that integrates offline exact Nash equilibrium computation with online tree search: PGTS first solves a collection of smaller, tractable sub-games offline; at deployment, PGTS performs online tree search at each time step, using the optimal sub-game policies and value functions to guide tree expansion and estimate leaf-node values. Extensive experiments on varied graph topologies, including real-world networks, demonstrate that PGTS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art learning and heuristic baselines, while maintaining robust performance against adversaries.
tldr: This paper proposes a hybrid framework combining offline Nash equilibrium computation with online tree search for multi-agent pursuit-evasion games on graphs.
motivation: Computing Nash equilibrium policies in multi-agent pursuit-evasion games is challenging due to exponential state and action spaces; existing offline methods lack adaptability and online methods suffer from large branching factors.
method: The framework, PGTS, first solves smaller sub-games offline to obtain optimal policies and value functions, then uses them to guide online tree search at each time step.
result: Experiments on various graph topologies show PGTS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art learning and heuristic baselines and maintains robust performance against adversaries.
conclusion: PGTS effectively integrates offline and online planning for multi-agent games on graphs, achieving strong performance and robustness.

title: Proof-of-Continuity: A Temporal Model For Authority Propagation In Distributed Systems And Ai Agents
authors: Nicola Gallo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proof-of-Possession authorization models derive authority from the possession of artifacts such as tokens, credentials, or capabilities. This paper argues that possession is insufficient for discrete execution chains, whether they span multiple services or occur as separated steps within the same machine, because it does not guarantee preservation of the causal relationship between the origin of a request and the authority exercised at later steps. We introduce Proof-of-Continuity, a minimal authority-propagation discipline for the Provenance Identity Continuity (PIC) model, in which each execution step must be causally linked to the previous step and may only propagate a non-expansive subset of the authority received from the origin. It introduces Proof of Relationship, a single-hop causal primitive whose transitive composition is Proof-of-Continuity; these complement Proof-of-Possession rather than replace it. Under this model, the confused deputy condition cannot be satisfied as valid model behavior: any privilege exercised at a later step must already be present in the origin authority context. This is directly relevant to distributed systems and AI agents, where executors invoke tools and downstream services while holding multiple authority sources, so that the same authority/causality mismatch recurs across service boundaries. Under Proof-of-Continuity these sources may be carried together but are never merged into a combined authority, since each step is authorized only against the authority context of the lineage that caused it. This paper concerns authorization propagation rather than authentication: identity and authentication mechanisms such as OIDC, verifiable credentials, wallets, and workload identity remain complementary mechanisms for establishing the origin, while Proof-of-Continuity addresses how authority propagates after that origin exists.
tldr: This paper proposes a temporal authority propagation model for distributed systems and AI agents, focusing on causal continuity rather than possession-based authorization.
motivation: Current authorization models based on possession of tokens fail to preserve causal relationships across execution steps, leading to security vulnerabilities like the confused deputy problem.
method: The paper introduces Proof-of-Continuity, a discipline where each execution step must be causally linked to the previous step and can only propagate a non-expansive subset of the original authority, using a primitive called Proof of Relationship.
result: Under this model, the confused deputy condition cannot be satisfied as valid behavior, and authority sources are never merged but carried together along the lineage.
conclusion: Proof-of-Continuity provides a minimal authority-propagation discipline that complements existing authentication mechanisms, ensuring that authority remains causally tied to the origin.

title: SeedSmith: LLM-Driven Seed Synthesis For Directed Fuzzing
authors: Junmin Zhu, Siyu Liu, Jie Hu, Fabio Gritti, Ati Priya Bajaj, Hulin Wang, Wenbo Guo, Tiffany Bao, Christopher Kruegel, Giovanni Vigna
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Directed fuzzing steers fuzzers toward user-defined sink functions to identify vulnerabilities, but it frequently fails to trigger crashes even after long campaigns. We identify two challenges that prevent directed fuzzers from exposing crashes: incomplete static analysis of indirect calls, which leaves reachable paths invisible to distance-based guidance, and lack of semantic guidance for crash preconditions, which blind mutation cannot satisfy within practical time budgets. A natural intervention point is the initial seed corpus: seeds that encode the right control-flow path and satisfy key crash preconditions shift fuzzing from blind exploration to local refinement. Existing seed generation approaches address neither: grammar-based and format-driven methods produce structurally valid inputs with no sink awareness, while LLM-based methods either lack sink targeting or inherit static analysis limitations through one-shot prompting. We present SeedSmith, an agentic LLM pipeline that replicates a security analyst's workflow: starting from a sink, it iteratively explores the codebase, resolves indirect calls, identifies crash preconditions, and synthesizes concrete inputs that satisfy them. Because SeedSmith operates as a seed generation front-end, its seeds are fuzzer-agnostic and improve any downstream mutation-based fuzzer without modification. On Magma, fuzzers using SeedSmith seeds achieve geometric mean crash-time speedups of 11.51 times (AFL++) to 14.66 times (AFLGo) over default seeds. On ARVO, SeedSmith enables fuzzers to trigger 16 previously unreachable bugs spanning 10 projects with diverse input formats.
tldr: SeedSmith uses an LLM agent to synthesize seed inputs for directed fuzzing, significantly improving crash discovery speed.
motivation: Directed fuzzing often fails due to incomplete static analysis of indirect calls and lack of semantic guidance for crash preconditions.
method: An agentic LLM pipeline iteratively explores code, resolves indirect calls, identifies crash preconditions, and synthesizes concrete inputs.
result: On Magma, fuzzers using SeedSmith seeds achieve geometric mean crash-time speedups of 11.51x (AFL++) to 14.66x (AFLGo); on ARVO, it triggers 16 previously unreachable bugs.
conclusion: SeedSmith effectively generates sink-aware seeds that improve directed fuzzing performance across different fuzzers.

title: RaMark: Radioactive Watermarking For Generated Tabular Data
authors: Xin Che, Lingyang Chu, Qiqi Zhang, Xinyu Ma, Xuan Luo, Jian Pei
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in generative modeling have made generated tabular data a practical solution for privacy-sensitive data sharing, where watermarking enables ownership verification. However, existing watermarking methods fundamentally fail under retraining attacks, in which an adversary retrains a generative model on a watermarked dataset and regenerates high-utility data that no longer carries the watermark. We address this challenge by introducing radioactivity, the property that a watermark remains detectable after generative model retraining, and propose RaMark, a radioactive watermarking method that embeds a sinusoidal dependency as an intrinsic component of the data distribution. By coupling the watermark with the underlying distribution, RaMark ensures that any generative model preserving data utility also has to preserve the watermark. We theoretically show that with high probability removing watermark degrades utility and alters data distribution. Extensive experiments on two real-world tabular datasets, under a large-scale ownership verification setting with [MATH] independent data owners, demonstrate that RaMark achieves substantially stronger radioactivity than seven state-of-the-art methods and consistently outperforms them against both retraining and data modification attacks.
tldr: This paper proposes a radioactive watermarking method for generated tabular data to resist retraining attacks.
motivation: Existing watermarking methods fail under retraining attacks where an adversary retrains a generative model on watermarked data and removes the watermark.
method: RaMark embeds a sinusoidal dependency as an intrinsic component of the data distribution, ensuring that any generative model preserving data utility must also preserve the watermark.
result: Theoretical analysis shows that removing the watermark degrades utility and alters distribution; experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate strong radioactivity against retraining and data modification attacks.
conclusion: RaMark provides a robust watermarking solution for tabular data generation, outperforming existing methods in ownership verification under adversarial retraining.

title: Secret Scanner Agent: Extracting Secrets And Access Context From Unstructured Documents
authors: Zixiao Chen, Mariko Wakabayashi, Charlotte Siska
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Exposed documents such as emails, chat threads, tickets, and incident notes routinely leak credentials, but during incident response a leaked secret is only half the story. Responders also need to identify the ``door'' the secret opens: the account, tenant, endpoint, database, cloud resource, or other system that the credential could allow an attacker to access. Traditional secret scanners rely on regular expressions or trained classifiers which work well on well-formatted code, yet they struggle when a credential is fragmented, reformatted, or far from the resource it unlocks, and they report the secret string without naming what it opens. We present Secret Scanner Agent (SSA), a multi-agent large-language-model system that extracts both the secret and its associated door, together with supporting evidence, from unstructured exposed documents. SSA pairs a detection agent that favors recall with a review agent that filters false positives and recovers missing context. Because real credential data is sensitive, we evaluate SSA on synthetic benchmarks we generated that span 23 secret types and multiple document formats, scored with a three-step pipeline of programmatic matching, an LLM judge, and human review. Across six models, multi-agent SSA improves extraction precision over a single-agent variant, with the largest gains on door extraction, by up to 16 percentage points. SSA matches a regular-expression scanner's precision while more than tripling its recall, and against thirteen security analysts it is more precise, recovers nearly twice as many secret--door pairs, and runs five to seventeen times faster. By returning the secret, its door, and supporting evidence in one result, SSA turns credential detection into an actionable finding for triage and remediation.
tldr: A multi-agent LLM system for extracting credentials and their associated access context from unstructured documents.
motivation: Traditional secret scanners fail on unstructured text and do not identify which resource a leaked credential unlocks, hindering incident response.
method: Uses a detection agent for high recall and a review agent to filter false positives and recover missing context, evaluated on synthetic benchmarks with programmatic matching, LLM judge, and human review.
result: Multi-agent SSA improves extraction precision over single-agent by up to 16 percentage points, matches regex precision while tripling recall, and outperforms human analysts in speed and accuracy.
conclusion: SSA turns credential detection into actionable findings by returning the secret, its door, and supporting evidence, enabling efficient triage and remediation.

title: Optimal Metric Distortion For Learning-Augmented Matching On The Line
authors: Marena Richter Jabari Hastings
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09038v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the problem of matching on the line with ordinal preferences. In the classic setting, there are [MATH] agents and [MATH] items in a shared unknown line metric, and the goal is to find a low-cost perfect matching using only the agents' rankings of the items by distance. A mechanism has distortion [MATH] if it always outputs a matching whose cost is within a factor of [MATH] of the optimum, in every consistent line metric. In the learning-augmented setting, the mechanism is also supplied with a prediction that conveys additional information about the instance. The quality of this prediction is unknown, and the goal is to optimize the mechanism's distortion when the prediction is accurate (consistency), while preserving worst-case guarantees when the prediction is arbitrarily inaccurate (robustness). We propose a mechanism that takes a matching as its prediction and guarantees [MATH]-consistency and [MATH]-robustness. By recovering an optimal matching when the prediction is perfectly accurate while retaining the optimal prediction-free distortion guarantee when it is arbitrarily inaccurate, we resolve an open question of Filos-Ratsikas et al. (IJCAI, 2025).
tldr: This paper studies the metric distortion of learning-augmented matching on the line with ordinal preferences, which is a problem in algorithmic game theory and mechanism design, not quantum information theory.
motivation: The paper aims to design a matching mechanism that leverages predictions to improve performance while maintaining worst-case guarantees, addressing an open question in the learning-augmented algorithms literature.
method: The authors propose a mechanism that takes a matching as a prediction and achieves 3-consistency and 3-robustness, using ordinal preferences only.
result: The mechanism recovers an optimal matching when the prediction is perfectly accurate and retains the optimal prediction-free distortion guarantee when the prediction is arbitrarily inaccurate.
conclusion: The work resolves an open question by providing a mechanism with optimal consistency and robustness trade-offs for matching on the line with ordinal preferences.

title: SherAgent: Scaling Attack Investigation In The Wild Via LLM-Empowered Iterative Query-Filter Backtracking
authors: Zhenyuan Li, Zhengkai Wang, Ling Jiang, Xiangmin Shen, Ruixiao Lin, Sen Nie, Shi Wu, Shouling Ji
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09176v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Provenance-based attack investigation enables viable automation by standardizing data and query logic; however, it is critically hindered in practice by dependency explosions and fragmented causal chains in the wild. Towards designing a robust and automated investigation tool, we collaborated with the SOC of a major Internet corporation serving billions of users. By engaging in real-world incident response, we are able to evaluate and refine their existing LLM-based investigation workflows, which processes tens of thousands of raw alerts daily, leaving thousands for manual triage, to find out the root causes of investigation failures and major challenges in their existing tools. Motivated by these findings, we propose SherAgent, an LLM-empowered automated investigation system. Operating on an iterative ``query-filter'' backtracking paradigm over provenance graphs, SherAgent leverages the semantic reasoning capabilities of LLMs to process unstructured data, such as investigation context and threat intelligence. To overcome fragmented causal chains caused by missing events, the system dynamically calibrates query conditions to broaden the search scope. Concurrently, it performs precision result filtering and strategic nodes selection for subsequent exploration, thereby mitigating dependency explosions. Extensive evaluations in the wild demonstrate that SherAgent improves the end-to-end investigation success rate by 31.1% and 63.7% compared to both legacy enterprise baselines and SOTA approaches, respectively. Furthermore, it operates with remarkable efficiency, incurring under $0.10 in API costs and requiring less than 4 minutes per investigation. Finally, our user study confirms that SherAgent provides accurate and clear insights, significantly reducing the analytical overhead for security experts.
tldr: This paper presents an LLM-empowered automated system for provenance-based attack investigation in cybersecurity.
motivation: Existing provenance-based attack investigation tools suffer from dependency explosions and fragmented causal chains, hindering automation in real-world security operations.
method: SherAgent uses an iterative query-filter backtracking paradigm over provenance graphs, leveraging LLMs for semantic reasoning to process unstructured data and dynamically calibrate query conditions.
result: SherAgent improves end-to-end investigation success rate by 31.1% over legacy baselines and 63.7% over SOTA approaches, with low cost and time per investigation.
conclusion: The system effectively reduces analytical overhead for security experts and demonstrates practical viability in large-scale enterprise environments.

title: Malaika: Understanding Malware Through Tri-Grounded Agentic Reasoning
authors: Xingzhi Qian, Xinran Zheng, Yiling He, Lorenzo Cavallaro
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09179v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent LLM-based systems have shown promising capabilities for security-focused code analysis. Malware understanding, however, poses a distinct challenge: analysts must reconstruct high-level malicious behaviors under partial observability from sparse, dispersed evidence intertwined with benign functionality. While static analysis can expose security-relevant signals, the central challenge is not merely identifying suspicious code, but determining whether the evidence sufficiently supports an auditable behavior-level conclusion. We formulate malware understanding as a grounded reasoning problem and argue that reliable behavior reconstruction requires three complementary forms of grounding. Domain grounding constrains how behavior hypotheses are generated and evaluated, semantics grounding localizes and connects supporting program evidence, and knowledge grounding supports behavioral attribution through externally verifiable threat knowledge. To study this hypothesis, we present Malaika, a multi-agent framework that operationalizes the three grounding mechanisms through analyst-inspired reasoning, tool-mediated evidence localization, and retrieval-based behavioral attribution. We instantiate Malaika for Android malware analysis and evaluate it on malware-understanding tasks. Results show that Malaika improves analysis quality over prior LLM-based malware-analysis frameworks and demonstrate that reliability depends not only on model capability but also on the reasoning process. In particular, comparisons against malware-analysis systems and frontier agentic frameworks show that grounding-aware reasoning produces more precise and auditable conclusions. Ablation studies further support the grounding hypothesis. These findings suggest that grounding-aware reasoning provides a principled foundation for reliable malware understanding and, more broadly, for evidence-grounded software analysis.
tldr: This paper presents Malaika, a multi-agent framework for malware understanding using tri-grounded agentic reasoning.
motivation: Malware understanding is challenging due to partial observability and intertwined benign functionality; existing LLM-based systems lack reliable behavior reconstruction.
method: Malaika operationalizes three grounding mechanisms (domain, semantics, knowledge) through multi-agent reasoning, tool-mediated evidence localization, and retrieval-based attribution.
result: Malaika improves analysis quality over prior LLM-based frameworks, showing that grounding-aware reasoning produces more precise and auditable conclusions.
conclusion: Grounding-aware reasoning provides a principled foundation for reliable malware understanding and evidence-grounded software analysis.

title: Leveraging Interpretable Tsetlin Machine For Pdf Malware Detection
authors: Rahul Jaiswal
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09290v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the digital era, Portable Document Format (PDF) is one of the most widely used file formats for storing and exchanging digital documents due to its platform independence and rich functionality. However, these same capabilities have also made PDF files an attractive attack vector for cyberattackers, who embed malicious code within seemingly legitimate documents to compromise target systems. This paper presents a novel interpretable Tsetlin Machine (TM)-based framework for PDF malware detection. The proposed framework extracts salient features from PDF documents through static analysis without executing the files and employs rule-based learning to accurately classify benign and malicious PDF documents. Numerical evaluation on the RIT-PDFMal-2026 dataset demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves competitive performance, attaining an accuracy of 98.02% compared with several ML classifiers and existing methods. Moreover, the proposed framework provides intrinsic interpretability by transparently explaining its classification decisions. The combination of competitive detection performance, computational efficiency, and intrinsic interpretability makes the proposed framework a promising solution for practical PDF malware detection.
tldr: This paper applies Tsetlin Machine to PDF malware detection, achieving high accuracy with interpretability.
motivation: PDF files are widely used and often exploited for malware; existing detection methods lack interpretability.
method: The framework extracts features via static analysis and uses rule-based Tsetlin Machine learning for classification.
result: The method achieves 98.02% accuracy on the RIT-PDFMal-2026 dataset, outperforming several ML classifiers.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a promising combination of performance, efficiency, and interpretability for practical PDF malware detection.

title: Sfds: Selective File Disclosure System
authors: Aditya Mitra, Quazi Fariha Tasnim, Hristina Mihajloska Trpcheska
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Access control to networked resources has been a longstanding challenge. The conventional solution relies on authentication mechanisms, which introduce additional complexities associated with Identity and Access Management (IAM). Such systems require user authentication, identity management, and authorization services, while also introducing security risks arising from vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, or implementation flaws. Furthermore, different file formats employ different mechanisms for ensuring authenticity and integrity through digital signatures. For example, PDF documents support the PDF Advanced Electronic Signature (PAdES) standard, whereas plain text files typically lack a standardized mechanism for embedding digital signatures. This paper proposes an architecture based on the Selective Disclosure JSON Web Token (SD-JWT) standard for securely sharing read-only files. The proposed architecture embeds cryptographic signatures and integrity protection directly into the shared resource, providing verifiable authenticity without relying on complex IAM infrastructures, such as centralized user databases, authentication services, or authorization mechanisms. By eliminating these components, the proposed solution simplifies deployment while maintaining strong security guarantees for the distribution of immutable resources.
tldr: This paper proposes a file access control architecture using Selective Disclosure JSON Web Tokens (SD-JWT) to embed cryptographic signatures directly into shared files, eliminating the need for centralized IAM systems.
motivation: Traditional access control relies on complex Identity and Access Management (IAM) systems that introduce security risks and implementation overhead. Different file formats lack standardized mechanisms for embedding digital signatures, making verifiable authenticity challenging.
method: The architecture uses SD-JWT to embed cryptographic signatures and integrity protection directly into read-only files, enabling verifiable authenticity without centralized authentication or authorization services.
result: The proposed system simplifies deployment while maintaining strong security guarantees for immutable resource distribution, eliminating the need for user databases and authentication services.
conclusion: The SD-JWT-based approach provides a lightweight, secure alternative to conventional IAM for sharing read-only files, though it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Complexity Of The Graph Homomorphism Problem W.r.t. Degeneracy
authors: Grigorii Braulov, Nikolai Chukhin, Alexander S. Kulikov, Ivan Mihajlin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The graph homomorphism problem HOM is: given an [MATH]-vertex source graph [MATH] and an [MATH]-vertex target graph [MATH], is there a mapping from [MATH] to [MATH] that preserves edges? A straightforward brute-force algorithm for HOM has running time [MATH] and it is known that, under ETH, there are no [MATH] algorithms. In recent years, less restrictive graph parameters [MATH] have been identified that allow one to solve HOM in time [MATH]. Examples include treewidth, maximum degree, and track number. On the other hand, it is known that the chromatic number parameter is too small: under ETH, HOM cannot be solved in time [MATH]. We study the complexity of HOM in terms of the degeneracy of [MATH]. This is perhaps the most natural unresolved graph parameter between the known algorithmic and hardness regimes: on the one hand, each of bounded treewidth, bounded maximum degree, and bounded track number implies bounded degeneracy; on the other hand, bounded degeneracy implies bounded chromatic number. Our results show that, at the same time, the influence of degeneracy of [MATH] on the complexity of HOM differs significantly from that of the previously studied parameters. We show that, under ETH, there is no [MATH] algorithm for any value of [MATH] as a function of [MATH]. We also show that bounded degeneracy alone does not make target size benign: even targets with [MATH] at most [MATH] and quasi-polynomial size force [MATH]-scale hardness. Finally, we introduce a no-compression barrier that explains why the known fine-grained lower bounds for sparse [MATH]-CSP are not tight under ETH. Moreover, it shows that substantially stronger lower bounds for polynomial-target degeneracy are unlikely to follow from standard reductions from sparse [MATH]-SAT.
tldr: This paper studies the complexity of the graph homomorphism problem parameterized by degeneracy, proving ETH-based lower bounds.
motivation: To understand the fine-grained complexity of graph homomorphism with respect to degeneracy, a parameter that lies between known algorithmic and hardness regimes.
method: The authors prove lower bounds under the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH) using reductions from sparse CSP and introduce a no-compression barrier.
result: Under ETH, there is no subexponential algorithm for graph homomorphism parameterized by degeneracy, and bounded degeneracy alone does not make target size benign.
conclusion: Degeneracy behaves differently from other parameters like treewidth or maximum degree, and stronger lower bounds are unlikely from standard reductions.

title: Closing The Complexity Gap For Exact Domatic Number At Three And Four
authors: Holger Spakowski
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09442v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The exact domatic-number problem asks, for a fixed integer k, whether a given graph G satisfies dom(G) = k. Riege and Rothe proved DP-completeness for every fixed k >= 5, while the cases k = 3 and k = 4 remained open. We close this classification gap. The main ingredient is a polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT whose output graphs have domatic number 4 in the satisfiable case and domatic number 2 in the unsatisfiable case; in particular, the reduction never produces a graph of domatic number 3. This directly realizes the route suggested by Riege and Rothe for closing the remaining cases. Together with a simpler three-versus-two reduction, this yields DP-completeness of Exact-3-DNP and Exact-4-DNP. The proofs are constructive and give explicit graph gadgets whose local domination constraints encode truth assignments and clause satisfaction. The soundness arguments show conversely that any sufficiently large domatic partition enforces the intended consistency conditions and therefore yields a satisfying assignment. Consequently, Exact-k-DNP is DP-complete for every fixed k >= 3, completing the fixed-value classification from k = 3 onward.
tldr: This paper proves DP-completeness for the exact domatic number problem for k=3 and k=4, closing a complexity gap.
motivation: The exact domatic number problem was known to be DP-complete for k>=5, but the cases k=3 and k=4 remained open. Closing this gap completes the fixed-value classification.
method: The paper presents a polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT to graphs where the domatic number is 4 if satisfiable and 2 if unsatisfiable, and a simpler reduction for the k=3 case.
result: Exact-3-DNP and Exact-4-DNP are DP-complete, thus Exact-k-DNP is DP-complete for every fixed k>=3.
conclusion: The complexity classification for the exact domatic number problem is now complete for all fixed k>=3.

title: Triggering Stealthy Feature Map Backdoors Via Physical Fault Injection In Embedded Neural Networks
authors: Steyn Hommes, Vincent Dankbaar, Tanguy Stekke, Xiaomeng Wang, Lisanne Weidmann, Senna van Hoek, Durba Chatterjee, Lejla Batina, Zhuoran Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09473v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fault injection (FI) attacks on embedded neural network (NN) implementations primarily focus on inducing misclassification by corrupting weights or intermediate computations, overlooking their interaction with algorithmic adversarial threats. In this work, we present a cross-level attack that bridges implementation-level physical faults to algorithm-level adversarial attacks. By characterizing fault-induced data perturbations during NN inference, we connect FI with backdoor learning, enabling system-level attacks that jointly exploit implementation- and algorithm-level vulnerabilities. Specifically, we propose a precise fault-injection method that reliably manipulates targeted register values to tractable states during execution. Leveraging this level of FI precision, we propose a novel end-to-end feature map-level backdoor attack, where physically induced intermediate perturbations serve as stealthy triggers. Unlike conventional input-based backdoors, our trigger is activated only under physical faults, causing the NN to exhibit adversarial behavior that compromises system integrity while remaining benign during normal operation. We demonstrate that such physically triggered backdoors can be mounted on embedded NN platforms and remain effective against existing backdoor defenses that typically assume input-space triggers. We showcase the attack practicality using electromagnetic FI on convolutional neural networks implemented on ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller, which is a common platform for constrained embedded applications. Our results highlight a novel attack vector at the intersection of hardware and algorithmic levels, stressing the need for defenses across abstraction levels.
tldr: This paper presents a cross-level attack that uses physical fault injection to trigger stealthy backdoors in embedded neural networks.
motivation: Fault injection attacks on neural networks typically cause misclassification, but this work explores how physical faults can be leveraged to create algorithmic backdoors that remain hidden during normal operation.
method: The authors characterize fault-induced data perturbations during inference and propose a precise fault-injection method to manipulate register values, enabling a feature map-level backdoor attack triggered only under physical faults.
result: The attack is demonstrated using electromagnetic fault injection on convolutional neural networks running on an ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller, showing effectiveness against existing backdoor defenses that assume input-space triggers.
conclusion: This work highlights a novel attack vector at the intersection of hardware and algorithmic security, stressing the need for cross-level defenses.

title: Solving The Reachability Problem For Branching Vector Addition Systems Via Semilinear Inductive Invariants
authors: Clotilde Bizi\`ere, J\'er\^ome Leroux, Gr\'egoire Sutre
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we solve the reachability problem for branching vector addition systems (BVAS), a long standing open problem. Our approach is based on semilinear inductive invariants. More precisely, we prove that if a configuration of a BVAS is not reachable, then there exists an inductive invariant, given as a semilinear set, that does not contain this configuration. Based on this property, we deduce a very simple (enumerative) algorithm solving the reachability problem for BVAS.
tldr: This paper solves the reachability problem for branching vector addition systems using semilinear inductive invariants.
motivation: The reachability problem for branching vector addition systems was a long-standing open problem in theoretical computer science.
method: The authors prove that if a configuration is not reachable, there exists a semilinear inductive invariant excluding it, leading to an enumerative algorithm.
result: They provide a complete solution to the reachability problem for BVAS.
conclusion: The work resolves a fundamental problem in formal verification and concurrency theory.

title: VEXAIoT: Autonomous IoT Vulnerability EXploitation Using Ai Agents
authors: Katherine Swinea, Kshitiz Aryal, Lopamudra Praharaj, Maanak Gupta
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) systems are inherently vulnerable due to constrained hardware, outdated firmware, and insecure default configurations, creating a need for scalable and adaptive security testing approaches. While recent adoptions of Large Language Model (LLM) agents have demonstrated promise in penetration testing and Capture-the-Flag (CTF) environments, their application to IoT specific vulnerabilities remains unexplored. This paper presents an autonomous multi-agent framework, referred to as Vulnerability EXploitation using AI Agents (VEXAIoT), for vulnerability discovery and exploitation in IoT environments using LLM-based reasoning and offensive security tools. The framework combines a vulnerability detection agent and an attack execution agent to perform reconnaissance, plan attack sequences, and execute exploits against vulnerable IoT services. The system is evaluated in IoTGoat and Metasploitable environments across ten attack scenarios mapped to OWASP IoT vulnerabilities. Experimental results show attack success rate of up to 100% with low token overhead and average execution times under two minutes for most attacks. Across 260 attack executions, VEXAIoT achieves a 95.0% overall success rate, including 94.5% success in IoTGoat and 96.7% success in Metasploitable2. These results demonstrate the potential for LLM-driven agents to automate IoT vulnerability assessment and offensive security workflows in controlled environments.
tldr: This paper presents an autonomous multi-agent framework using LLMs for vulnerability discovery and exploitation in IoT environments.
motivation: IoT systems are inherently vulnerable, and there is a need for scalable and adaptive security testing approaches.
method: The framework combines a vulnerability detection agent and an attack execution agent to perform reconnaissance, plan attack sequences, and execute exploits against vulnerable IoT services.
result: The system achieves up to 100% attack success rate with low token overhead and average execution times under two minutes, with a 95.0% overall success rate across 260 attack executions.
conclusion: LLM-driven agents can automate IoT vulnerability assessment and offensive security workflows in controlled environments.

title: Impact Of Benign Connectivity Variations On Intrusion Detection For Encrypted Opc Ua Traffic In Industrial Private 5g Networks
authors: Song Son Ha, Florian Foerster, Henry Beuster, Tim Kittel, Dominik Merli, Gerd Scholl
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning (ML)-based intrusion detection systems (IDSs) are increasingly used to monitor encrypted industrial communication. However, their behavior under realistic private 5G operating conditions remains insufficiently understood. This paper investigates the impact of benign connectivity variations on ML-based IDSs for encrypted Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture (OPC UA) traffic in industrial private 5G networks. Experimental results show that legitimate connectivity events can noticeably increase false positive activity despite the absence of attacks. Furthermore, elevated IDS anomaly scores frequently coincide with periods of control-plane (CP) activity associated with these events. The findings highlight the importance of considering CP context when interpreting IDS outputs in industrial private 5G environments.
tldr: This paper studies the impact of benign connectivity variations on ML-based intrusion detection for encrypted OPC UA traffic in industrial private 5G networks.
motivation: ML-based IDS are used for encrypted industrial communication, but their behavior under realistic private 5G conditions is not well understood.
method: Experimental evaluation of ML-based IDS on encrypted OPC UA traffic in a private 5G testbed, analyzing false positive rates and anomaly scores during benign connectivity events.
result: Legitimate connectivity events increase false positive activity, and elevated anomaly scores coincide with control-plane activity.
conclusion: Control-plane context should be considered when interpreting IDS outputs in industrial private 5G environments.

title: Convergence Of Fictitious Play For Fully Coupled FBSDEs In Finite-player Stochastic Differential Games
authors: Adam Andersson, Kristoffer Andersson, Per Ljung
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08861v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article we investigate the theoretical convergence properties of the fictitious-play approximation procedure applied to coupled FBSDE systems for finite-player non-zero-sum stochastic differential games. Under one set of assumptions, the convergence is shown to be geometric. Under an additional structural assumption, the geometric convergence rate further improves to a super-exponential rate in a special class of games. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first convergence analysis of fictitious play for fully coupled FBSDEs. A numerical experiment with a linear-quadratic interbank borrowing and lending problem confirms the geometric convergence.
tldr: This paper analyzes convergence of fictitious play for fully coupled forward-backward stochastic differential equations in finite-player stochastic differential games.
motivation: To provide the first convergence analysis of fictitious play for fully coupled FBSDEs, which are important in game theory and control.
method: The authors prove geometric convergence under one set of assumptions and super-exponential convergence under an additional structural assumption, supported by a numerical experiment.
result: Geometric convergence is established generally, and super-exponential convergence is shown for a special class of games.
conclusion: The fictitious play procedure converges for fully coupled FBSDEs, with rates depending on problem structure.

title: Privacy Detective: A Narrative Game That Cultivates Student Developers' Privacy Awareness By Harnessing Legal Documents
authors: Shao-Yu Chu, Jennifer Forsyth, Xu Wang, Haojian Jin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.09022v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Developers' choices about what data a system collects, how it is used and shared, and what defaults govern user choices directly shape users' privacy experiences. Yet, developers often make problematic privacy-related design decisions without realizing the potential consequences. We introduce Privacy Detective, a narrative investigation game that leverages real-world legal documents to train developers' privacy awareness. In the game, players search for privacy violation evidence derived from legal documents and organize this evidence into privacy violation reports using curated templates. We evaluated Privacy Detective in a between-subjects study with student developers, comparing it against a baseline in which participants read raw FTC legal documents. Participants in the game condition identified more true violations than the baseline group, flagged fewer non-issues, and provided more complete justifications for the violations they reported.
tldr: A narrative game that uses legal documents to train student developers' privacy awareness.
motivation: Developers often make poor privacy decisions; the paper aims to improve privacy awareness through an engaging educational tool.
method: Privacy Detective game where players search for privacy violations in legal documents and organize evidence into reports; evaluated via between-subjects study.
result: Game condition participants identified more true violations, flagged fewer non-issues, and provided more complete justifications than baseline.
conclusion: The game effectively cultivates privacy awareness in student developers compared to reading raw legal documents.
